title.zh: 卷四百〇一 列傳第一百六十 辛棄疾 何異 劉宰 劉爚 柴中行 李孟傳
title.en: Volume 401 Biographies 160: Xin Qiji, He Yi, Liu Zai, Liu Yue, Chai Zhongxing, Li Mengchuan
title.raw: 卷四百〇一 列傳第一百六十 辛棄疾 何異 劉宰 劉爚 柴中行 李孟傳 Volume 401 Biographies 160: Xin Qiji, He Yi, Liu Zai, Liu Yue, Chai Zhongxing, Li Mengchuan

sentences.zh: 辛棄疾 何異 劉宰 劉爚 柴中行 李孟傳

translations.literal: Xin Qiji, He Yi, Liu Zai, Liu Yue, Chai Zhongxing, Li Mengchuan
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji, He Yi, Liu Zai, Liu Yue, Chai Zhongxing, and Li Mengchuan

sentences.zh: 辛棄疾

translations.literal: Xin Qiji
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji

sentences.zh: 辛棄疾，字幼安，齊之曆城人。

translations.literal: Xin Qiji, styled You'an, was a man of Licheng in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji, whose courtesy name was You'an, came from Licheng in Qi.

sentences.zh: 少師蔡伯堅，與党懷英同學，號「辛黨」。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Cai Bojian; he studied together with Dang Huaiying and they were called the "Xin–Dang" pair.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he took Cai Bojian as his teacher and studied alongside Dang Huaiying; the two were known together as the "Xin–Dang" pair.

sentences.zh: 始筮仕，決以蓍，懷英遇《坎》，因留事金，棄疾得《離》，遂決意南歸。

translations.literal: When they first divined on taking office, they decided by yarrow stalks: Huaiying obtained Kan and therefore remained to serve Jin; Qiji obtained Li and thereupon resolved to return south.
translations.idiomatic: When they first sought divination about entering government service, they cast yarrow stalks to decide: Huaiying drew the hexagram Kan and stayed on to serve the Jin; Qiji drew Li and at once made up his mind to go south to Song.

sentences.zh: 金主亮死，中原豪傑並起。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Hailing died, heroes of the Central Plains rose together.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin emperor Hailing was killed, champions across the Central Plains rose up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 耿京聚兵山東，稱天平節度使，節制山東、河北忠義軍馬，棄疾為掌書記，即勸京決策南向。

translations.literal: Geng Jing gathered troops in Shandong, styled himself Military Commissioner of Heavenly Peace, and controlled the loyalist forces of Shandong and Hebei; Qiji served as his registrar and at once urged Jing to decide on a southern strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jing mustered forces in Shandong, took the title Military Commissioner of Heavenly Peace, and commanded the loyalist armies of Shandong and Hebei; Xin Qiji served as his chief secretary and immediately urged Jing to commit to marching south.

sentences.zh: 僧義端者，喜談兵，棄疾間與之遊。

translations.literal: There was a monk named Yiduan who delighted in discussing warfare; Qiji would occasionally associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Yiduan loved to talk of military affairs, and Xin Qiji would now and then keep his company.

sentences.zh: 及在京軍中，義端亦聚眾千餘，說下之，使隸京。

translations.literal: When Yiduan was in Jing's army, he also gathered more than a thousand followers; Qiji persuaded him to submit and had him placed under Jing's command.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yiduan was in Geng Jing's camp, he too rallied more than a thousand men; Xin Qiji talked him into yielding and had him attached to Jing's command.

sentences.zh: 義端一夕竊印以逃，京大怒，欲殺棄疾。

translations.literal: One night Yiduan stole the seal and fled; Jing was greatly enraged and wished to kill Qiji.
translations.idiomatic: One night Yiduan stole the command seal and fled; Geng Jing was furious and meant to execute Xin Qiji.

sentences.zh: 棄疾曰：「丐我三日期，不獲，就死未晚。」

translations.literal: Qiji said: "Grant me three days; if I do not capture him, it will not be too late for me to die."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji said, "Give me three days—if I fail to take him, it will not be too soon for me to die."

sentences.zh: 揣僧必以虛實奔告金帥，急追獲之。

translations.literal: He reckoned the monk would surely report the army's strengths and weaknesses to the Jin commander and pursued him urgently, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: He judged that the monk would surely run to the Jin commander with every detail of the army's condition, gave hot pursuit, and seized him.

sentences.zh: 義端曰：「我識君真相，乃青兕也，力能殺人，幸勿殺我。」

translations.literal: Yiduan said: "I know your true form—you are the Blue Buffalo; your strength can kill men; I beg you not to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Yiduan cried, "I know your true nature—you are the Blue Buffalo, with strength enough to kill a man; spare me, I beg you."

sentences.zh: 棄疾斬其首歸報，京益壯之。

translations.literal: Qiji cut off his head and returned to report; Jing admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji struck off his head and brought it back in report; Geng Jing thought all the more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年，京令棄疾奉表歸宋，高宗勞師建康，召見，嘉納之，授承務郎、天平節度掌書記，並以節使印告召京。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, Jing ordered Qiji to present a memorial and return to Song; Gaozong received the army at Jiankang, summoned him, praised and accepted him, appointed him Gentleman for Palace Service and registrar to the Military Commissioner of Heavenly Peace, and also used the commissioner's seal to summon Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing (1162), Geng Jing sent Xin Qiji to present a memorial and return to the Song court; Emperor Gaozong received the troops at Jiankang, summoned him, praised his mission, and appointed him Gentleman for Palace Service and registrar to the Military Commissioner of Heavenly Peace, while also using the commissioner's seal to summon Geng Jing.

sentences.zh: 會張安國、邵進已殺京降金，棄疾還至海州，與眾謀曰：「我緣主帥來歸朝，不期事變，何以復命？」

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Anguo and Shao Jin had already killed Jing and surrendered to Jin; Qiji returned to Haizhou and consulted the company, saying: "I came to the court on account of our commander; I did not expect events to change—how am I to answer for my mission?"
translations.idiomatic: But Zhang Anguo and Shao Jin had already murdered Geng Jing and gone over to the Jin; when Xin Qiji reached Haizhou he told the men, "I came to court for our commander's sake; I never expected things to turn out like this—how can I report back?"

sentences.zh: 乃約統制王世隆及忠義人馬全福等徑趨金營，安國方與金將酣飲，即眾中縛之以歸，金將追之不及。

translations.literal: Thereupon he agreed with Controller Wang Shilong and the loyalist Ma Quanfu and others to strike straight at the Jin camp; Anguo was just drinking freely with a Jin general when they bound him in the midst of the crowd and carried him off; the Jin general pursued but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Controller Wang Shilong and loyalists such as Ma Quanfu in a dash straight into the Jin camp; Zhang Anguo was still drinking with a Jin officer when they seized him in the throng and hauled him away, and though Jin troops gave chase they could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 獻俘行在，斬安國於市。

translations.literal: He presented the captive at the imperial camp and executed Anguo in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the prisoner at the traveling palace and had Anguo beheaded in public.

sentences.zh: 仍授前官，改差江陰僉判。

translations.literal: He was still granted his former office and reassigned as assistant magistrate of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his former rank and was reassigned as assistant prefect of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 棄疾時年二十三。

translations.literal: Qiji was then twenty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji was twenty-three years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年，通判建康府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiandao (1168) he served as vice prefect of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiandao (1168) he was made vice prefect of Jiankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，孝宗召對延和殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Xiaozong Emperor summoned him for audience in the Yanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Emperor Xiaozong received him in audience in the Yanhe Hall.

sentences.zh: 時虞允文當國，帝銳意恢復，棄疾因論南北形勢及三國、晉、漢人才，持論勁直，不為迎合。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Yunwen held power and the emperor was keen on recovery; Qiji discussed the strategic situation north and south and the talents of the Three Kingdoms, Jin, and Han periods; his arguments were forceful and direct and he did not trim his views to please.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen was then directing the government and the emperor was eager to recover lost territory; Xin Qiji spoke on the strategic balance between north and south and on talent in the eras of the Three Kingdoms, the Jin, and the Han; his views were blunt and forceful, and he would not soften them to please.

sentences.zh: 作《九議》並《應問》三篇、《美芹十論》獻於朝，言逆順之理，消長之勢，技之長短，地之要害，甚備。

translations.literal: He composed the "Nine Discourses," three chapters of "Responses to Questions," and the "Ten Discourses of Beautiful Celery" and presented them to court, setting forth the principles of compliance and resistance, the waxing and waning of power, the strengths and weaknesses of tactics, and critical points of terrain, in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Nine Discourses, three chapters of Responses to Questions, and the Ten Discourses of Beautiful Celery and submitted them to court, treating in full the logic of submission versus resistance, the ebb and flow of power, the strengths and limits of strategy, and the decisive points of terrain.

sentences.zh: 以講和方定，議不行。

translations.literal: Because peace negotiations had just been settled, his proposals were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks had only just been concluded, however, and his plans were not put into effect.

sentences.zh: 遷司農寺主簿，出知滁州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent out as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to registrar in the Directorate of Agriculture and appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 州罹兵燼，井邑凋殘，棄疾寬征薄賦，招流散，教民兵，議屯田，乃創奠枕樓、繁雄館。

translations.literal: The prefecture had suffered the ravages of war; towns and villages were desolate; Qiji eased levies and lightened taxes, recalled the displaced, trained militia, discussed garrison farming, and thereupon founded the Pillow-Rest Tower and the Flourishing-Heroes Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had been scorched by war and its towns lay in ruins; Xin Qiji reduced levies and lightened taxes, summoned back refugees, drilled militia, promoted garrison farming, and built the Pillow-Rest Tower and the Flourishing-Heroes Hall.

sentences.zh: 辟江東安撫司參議官。

translations.literal: He was invited as planning officer of the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as planning officer on the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 留守葉衡雅重之，衡入相，力薦棄疾慷慨有大略。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Ye Heng held him in high esteem; when Heng entered the council he strongly recommended Qiji as magnanimous and possessed of great strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Ye Heng valued him highly; when Ye entered the chief council he urged that Xin Qiji was open-handed and possessed of grand design.

sentences.zh: 召見，遷倉部郎官、提點江西刑獄。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue and made judicial intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 平劇盜賴文政有功，加秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing the great bandit Lai Wenzheng he was given the additional title Academician of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing the major bandit Lai Wenzheng he received the additional title Academician of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 調京西轉運判官，差知江陵府兼湖北安撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Transport Judge of Jingxi and appointed prefect of Jiangling while also serving as pacification commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport judge of Jingxi and appointed prefect of Jiangling while doubling as pacification commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 遷知隆興府兼江西安撫，以大理少卿召，出為湖北轉運副使，改湖南，尋知潭州兼湖南安撫。

translations.literal: He was moved to prefect of Longxing while also Jiangxi pacification commissioner; summoned as Vice Minister of Justice, he went out as deputy transport commissioner of Hubei, then Hunan, and soon became prefect of Tanzhou while also Hunan pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Longxing with concurrent duty as Jiangxi pacification commissioner; summoned as vice minister of justice, he went out as deputy transport commissioner of Hubei, then of Hunan, and soon held Tanzhou as prefect while also serving as Hunan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 盜連起湖湘，棄疾悉討平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in succession in the lakes and Xiang region; Qiji suppressed and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands broke out one after another across the lake country and the Xiang basin; Xin Qiji hunted them down and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 遂奏疏曰：「今朝廷清明，比年李金、賴文政、陳子明、陳峒相繼竊發，皆能一呼嘯聚千百，殺掠吏民，死且不顧，至煩大兵翦滅。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial saying: "The court today is enlightened; yet in recent years Li Jin, Lai Wenzheng, Chen Ziming, and Chen Dong have risen in succession; each could summon hundreds or thousands with a single shout, slaughter officials and people, and face death without flinching, until great armies had to be sent to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne: "The court is enlightened today, yet in recent years Li Jin, Lai Wenzheng, Chen Ziming, and Chen Dong have broken out in turn—each could rally hundreds or thousands at a cry, kill officials and commoners, and meet death unafraid, until imperial troops had to be sent to wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 良由州以趣辦財賦為急，吏有殘民害物之狀，而州不敢問，縣以並緣科斂為急，吏有殘民害物之狀，而縣不敢問。

translations.literal: Truly because prefectures are pressed to raise revenue, officials have records of harming the people yet the prefecture dares not inquire; counties are pressed to levy surcharges, officials have records of harming the people yet the county dares not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is that prefectures are driven to hurry revenue collection: clerks have records of preying on the people, yet the prefecture does not dare investigate; counties are driven to squeeze extra levies: clerks have records of preying on the people, yet the county does not dare investigate.

sentences.zh: 田野之民，郡以聚斂害之，縣以科率害之，吏以乞取害之，豪民以兼併害之，盜賊以剽奪害之，民不為盜，去將安之？

translations.literal: For the people of field and village, the commandery harms them by exactions, the county harms them by assessments, clerks harm them by extortion, powerful families harm them by encroachment, bandits harm them by plunder—if the people do not become bandits, where can they go?
translations.idiomatic: In the countryside the commandery injures them through exaction, the county through assessments, clerks through squeezing, powerful families through swallowing up land, and bandits through robbery—if the people do not turn bandit, where else can they turn?

sentences.zh: 夫民為國本，而貪吏迫使為盜，今年剿除，明年劃蕩，譬之木焉，日刻月削，不損則折。

translations.literal: The people are the root of the state, yet greedy officials drive them to become bandits; they are wiped out this year and swept away the next—like a tree, carved month by month, if not diminished it will break.
translations.idiomatic: The people are the foundation of the state, yet greedy officials force them into banditry; we exterminate them one year and scour them the next—as with a tree, whittled day by day, it must snap if the cutting never stops.

sentences.zh: 欲望陛下深思致盜之由，講求弭盜之術，無徒恃平盜之兵。

translations.literal: I desire Your Majesty to ponder deeply the causes that produce bandits and to seek means to quell banditry, and not merely rely on troops that merely pacify bandits.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think hard about what breeds bandits and to work out how to end banditry, instead of trusting only to armies sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 申飭州縣，以惠養元元為意，有違法貪冒者，使諸司各揚其職，無徒按舉小吏以應故事，自為文過之地。」

translations.literal: Charge prefectures and counties to treat nourishing the people as their purpose; where officials violate law and grasp for gain, let each department perform its duty and not merely impeach petty clerks to satisfy form, making a place to paper over faults."
translations.idiomatic: Instruct prefectures and counties to make cherishing the people their aim; where officials break the law and grab illicit gain, let every agency do its proper work and not merely indict minor clerks to tick boxes, thereby giving themselves room to hide their own failures."

sentences.zh: 詔獎諭之。

translations.literal: An edict praised and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict praising and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 又以湖南控帶二廣，與溪峒蠻獠接連，草竊間作，豈惟風俗頑悍，抑武備空虛所致。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Hunan borders the Two Guang and connects with the Man and Liao of streams and ravines, with sporadic grass-roots uprisings, it was not only that local customs were stubborn and fierce but also that military preparations were hollow.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Hunan flanks the Two Guang and adjoins the tribal peoples of the gorges, where petty risings broke out from time to time—not only because the people were unruly, but because defenses had been left empty.

sentences.zh: 乃復奏疏曰：「軍政之敝，統率不一，差出占破，略無已時。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "The ills of military administration are that command is not unified and detachments are seconded and encroached upon without end.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Military administration is sick because there is no single chain of command and detachments are borrowed away piecemeal without cease.

sentences.zh: 軍人則利於優閑窠坐，奔走公門，苟圖衣食，以故教閱廢弛，逃亡者不追，冒名者不舉。

translations.literal: Soldiers profit from easy idleness and cushioned posts, running to government offices to scrape together food and clothing; thus drill and review are abandoned, deserters are not pursued, and false names on the rolls are not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The troops prefer easy berths and cushioned billets, haunt government offices to scrape a living, and so training falls into neglect—deserters go unrecovered and men listed under false names go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 平居則奸民無所忌憚，緩急則卒伍不堪征行。

translations.literal: In ordinary times wicked men have nothing to fear; in emergencies the ranks cannot bear to be mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime ruffians have nothing to fear; when crisis comes the ranks cannot march.

sentences.zh: 至調大軍，千里討捕，勝負未決，傷威損重，為害非細。

translations.literal: When great armies are mobilized for pursuit a thousand li away, victory and defeat hang unresolved, prestige is injured and weight is lost—the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: When large forces must be sent a thousand li to hunt bandits, victory is uncertain, prestige suffers, and the cost is grave.

sentences.zh: 乞依廣東摧鋒、荊南神勁、福建左翼例，別創一軍，以湖南飛虎為名，止撥屬三牙、密院，專聽帥臣節制調度，庶使夷獠知有軍威，望風懾服。」

translations.literal: I beg that following the examples of Guangdong's Crushing Vanguard, Jingnan's Divine Striking Force, and Fujian's Left Wing, a separate army be created named the Hunan Flying Tiger, assigned only to the three bureaus and the Privy Council and placed solely under the pacification commissioner's command and deployment, so that the tribes may know there is military might and submit at the sight of it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, following Guangdong's Crushing Vanguard, Jingnan's Divine Striking Force, and Fujian's Left Wing, a new army be formed—the Hunan Flying Tiger—reporting only to the three bureaus and the Privy Council and taking orders solely from the pacification commissioner, so that the hill peoples know there is real force on the border and tremble at the name."

sentences.zh: 詔委以規畫，乃度馬殷營壘故基，起蓋砦柵，招步軍二千人，馬軍五百人，傔人在外，戰馬鐵甲皆備。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted him with planning; he measured the old encampment site of Ma Yin and built stockades, recruiting two thousand foot soldiers and five hundred horse soldiers, with attendants outside and war horses and iron armor all provided.
translations.idiomatic: The court authorized him to plan it; he surveyed the old camp grounds of Ma Yin, threw up stockades, recruited two thousand foot and five hundred horse, with servants quartered outside and war horses and iron armor fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 先以緡錢五萬于廣西買馬五百匹，詔廣西安撫司歲帶買三十匹。

translations.literal: First he used fifty thousand strings of cash to buy five hundred horses in Guangxi; an edict ordered the Guangxi Pacification Commission to purchase thirty horses annually on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He first spent fifty thousand strings of cash in Guangxi to buy five hundred horses; an edict directed the Guangxi Pacification Commission to buy thirty horses for him each year.

sentences.zh: 時樞府有不樂之者，數沮撓之，棄疾行愈力，卒不能奪。

translations.literal: At that time there were those in the Military Affairs Commission who disliked him and several times obstructed him; Qiji pressed on all the more and in the end they could not thwart him.
translations.idiomatic: Some at the Military Affairs Commission disliked him and tried repeatedly to block the project; Xin Qiji pushed harder still and in the end they could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 經度費钜萬計，棄疾善斡旋，事皆立辦。

translations.literal: The total cost ran to tens of thousands; Qiji was skilled at maneuvering and everything was set up at once.
translations.idiomatic: The undertaking cost a vast sum, but Xin Qiji was adept at cutting through red tape and had every item in place on schedule.

sentences.zh: 議者以聚斂聞，降御前金字牌，俾日下住罷。

translations.literal: Critics reported him for exaction; the court sent down an imperial golden plaque ordering him to halt immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Critics accused him of squeezing the region for funds; the court issued an imperial golden plaque ordering him to stop at once.

sentences.zh: 棄疾受而藏之，出責監辦者，期一月飛虎營柵成，違坐軍制。

translations.literal: Qiji received it and put it away, went out and rebuked the supervisors, fixing one month for completion of the Flying Tiger camp stockade—violation would be punished under military law.
translations.idiomatic: He took the plaque, locked it away, went out and scolded the overseers, and gave them one month to finish the Flying Tiger stockade—any breach would be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 如期落成，開陳本末，繪圖繳進，上遂釋然，時秋霖幾月，所司言造瓦不易，問：「須瓦幾何？」

translations.literal: When it was completed on schedule he set forth the whole account and submitted a diagram; the emperor was reassured; it had been raining for months that autumn and the offices said tiles were hard to make and asked: "How many tiles are needed?"
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline was met he laid out the full story and sent in a plan; the emperor relented. Rain had fallen for months that autumn, and the offices said roofing tiles would be hard to obtain and asked how many were needed.

sentences.zh: 曰：「二十萬。」

translations.literal: He said: "Two hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Two hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 棄疾曰：「勿憂。」

translations.literal: Qiji said: "Do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji said, "Do not worry."

sentences.zh: 令廂官自官舍、神祠外，應居民家取溝敢瓦二，不二日皆具，僚屬歎伏。

translations.literal: He ordered the ward officers, apart from official quarters and shrines, to take two tiles each from every household ditch—within two days all were ready and his staff marveled.
translations.idiomatic: He told the ward officers that, apart from government buildings and temples, every household should contribute two tiles from its ditches; within two days the quota was met and his subordinates were astonished.

sentences.zh: 軍成，雄鎮一方，為江上諸軍之冠。

translations.literal: When the army was formed it dominated the region and was the finest of the armies along the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When the force stood up it dominated the region and ranked first among the Yangzi armies.

sentences.zh: 加右文殿修撰，差知隆興府兼江西安撫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Academician of the Right Culture Hall and appointed prefect of Longxing while also Jiangxi pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title Academician of the Right Culture Hall and was appointed prefect of Longxing with concurrent duty as Jiangxi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時江右大饑，詔任責荒政。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangyou suffered great famine; an edict charged him with famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyou was then in severe famine; an edict put him in charge of famine relief.

sentences.zh: 始至，榜通衢曰：「閉糴者配，強糴者斬。」

translations.literal: As soon as he arrived he posted notices on the main thoroughfare: "Those who hoard grain shall be banished; those who force purchase shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he posted placards along the main roads: "Whoever hoards grain will be exiled; whoever forces a buy will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 次令盡出公家官錢、銀器，召官吏、儒生、商賈、市民各舉有幹實者，量借錢物，逮其責領運糴，不取子錢，期終月至城下發糶，於是連檣而至，其直自減，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Next he ordered all government cash and silver vessels released; he summoned officials, scholars, merchants, and townspeople each to nominate capable men, lent money and goods by measure, and had them take charge of transporting grain without interest, to reach the city within a month for sale—then grain boats came in succession, prices fell of themselves, and the people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: He next ordered every coin and silver vessel in the government stores released, called on officials, scholars, merchants, and townspeople each to name capable men, lent them funds and goods in measured amounts, and charged them to bring in grain without interest so that within a month supplies would reach the city for sale; grain boats then lined the river, prices fell on their own, and the people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 時信守謝源明乞米救助，幕屬不從，棄疾曰：「均為赤子，皆王民也。」

translations.literal: At that time Xie Yuanming of Xinyang begged grain for relief; staff members refused; Qiji said: "They are equally children of the realm, all subjects of the king."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yuanming of Xinyang asked for grain aid; his staff objected, but Xin Qiji said, "They are all the emperor's children alike."

sentences.zh: 即以米舟十之三予信。

translations.literal: He at once gave three tenths of the grain boats to Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately allotted three tenths of the grain fleet to Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，進一秩，以言者落職，久之，主管沖佑觀。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and advanced him one rank; because of critics he lost his post; after a long while he supervised the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and raised him one rank; critics then brought about his dismissal, and after a long interval he was put in charge of the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，起福建提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi (1191) he was recalled as Judicial Intendant of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxi (1191) he was recalled to serve as judicial intendant of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 召見，遷大理少卿，加集英殿修撰、知福州兼福建安撫使。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, given the additional title Academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence, and made prefect of Fuzhou while also Fujian pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he was made vice minister of justice, given the additional title Academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence, and appointed prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent duty as Fujian pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 棄疾為憲時，嘗攝帥，每歎曰：「福州前枕大海，為賊之淵，上四郡民頑獷易亂，帥臣空竭，急緩奈何！」

translations.literal: When Qiji had served as judicial commissioner he had also acted as commander and often sighed: "Fuzhou fronts the sea and is a lair of bandits; the four upper prefectures have stubborn, fierce people easy to stir to disorder—the commander exhausts himself with nothing in reserve; what is to be done in emergency or crisis?"
translations.idiomatic: While serving as intendant he had also acted as commander and often said, "Fuzhou faces the sea and is a nest of pirates; the four upper prefectures breed stubborn, unruly people who riot easily—the commander drains himself dry and has nothing in reserve; what happens when trouble comes?"

sentences.zh: 至是務為鎮靜，未期歲，積鏹至五十萬緡，榜曰：「備安庫」。

translations.literal: Now he devoted himself to calm rule; within less than a year accumulated cash reached five hundred thousand strings, and he posted it as the "Reserve-for-Peace Treasury."
translations.idiomatic: Now he set himself to steady administration; in less than a year he had amassed five hundred thousand strings of cash and labeled the fund the "Reserve-for-Peace Treasury."

sentences.zh: 謂閩中土狹民稠，歲儉則糴於廣，今幸連稔，宗室及軍人入倉請米，出即糶之，候秋賈賤，以備安錢糴二萬石，則有備無患矣。

translations.literal: He said that in Fujian the land was narrow and the people dense; in lean years they bought grain from Guang; now, fortunately, harvests had come in succession; when clansmen and soldiers drew rice from the granary they sold it at once; when autumn came and prices were low he would use the reserve funds to buy twenty thousand shi of grain, and then there would be provision against want.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Fujian's land was tight and its population thick; in bad years they bought grain from Guangdong; now that harvests had run fair, when clansmen and soldiers drew rations from the granary he sold the grain back immediately, and when autumn prices fell he would use the reserve to buy twenty thousand shi so the province would not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 又欲造萬鎧，招強壯補軍額，嚴訓練，則盜賊可以無虞。

translations.literal: He also wished to forge ten thousand suits of armor, recruit stalwarts to fill army rolls, and drill them strictly, so that bandits would have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to forge ten thousand suits of armor, recruit sturdy men to fill the rolls, and train them hard so that banditry would cease to be a worry.

sentences.zh: 事未行，台臣王藺劾其用錢如泥沙，殺人如草芥，旦夕望端坐「閩王殿」。

translations.literal: Before the matter was carried out, remonstrance official Wang Lin impeached him for spending money like sand and mud and killing men like grass and reeds, looking any day to take the seat in the "Hall of the King of Min."
translations.idiomatic: Before these plans could be enacted, remonstrance official Wang Lin accused him of spending money like sand and killing men like weeds, as though he meant any day to mount the throne in a "Hall of the King of Min."

sentences.zh: 遂丐祠歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon begged a temple post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon asked for a sinecure and went home.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年落職，四年，復主管沖佑觀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan (1195) he lost his post; in the fourth year he again supervised the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingyuan (1195) he was stripped of office; in the fourth year he again took charge of the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知紹興府兼浙東安撫使，四年，甯宗召見，言鹽法，加寶謨閣待制、提舉佑神觀，奉朝請。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled as prefect of Shaoxing while also Eastern Zhejiang pacification commissioner; in the fourth year Emperor Ningzong summoned him and he spoke on the salt law; he was given the additional title Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Planning, put in charge of the You-Shen Abbey, and made a court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as prefect of Shaoxing with concurrent duty as Eastern Zhejiang pacification commissioner; in the fourth year Emperor Ningzong received him and he addressed the salt monopoly; he was made Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Planning, placed in charge of the You-Shen Abbey, and given standing as a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋差知鎮江府，賜金帶。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Zhenjiang and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Zhenjiang and granted a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 坐繆舉，降朝散大夫、提舉沖佑觀，差知紹興府、兩浙東路安撫使，辭免。

translations.literal: For a faulty recommendation he was demoted to Grandee of Palace Accord, put in charge of the Chongyou Abbey, and offered the prefecture of Shaoxing and the Eastern Zhejiang pacification commission, which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: For a faulty recommendation he was demoted to Grandee of Palace Accord, put in charge of the Chongyou Abbey, and offered Shaoxing with the Eastern Zhejiang pacification commission, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 進寶文閣待制，又進龍圖閣、知江陵府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Literature and again to the Dragon Diagram Hall while serving as prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Literature and then to the Dragon Diagram Hall while holding Jiangling as prefect.

sentences.zh: 令赴行在奏事，試兵部侍郎，辭免。

translations.literal: Ordered to proceed to the capital to report, he was tested for Vice Minister of War and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to the capital to report, he was examined for vice minister of war and declined.

sentences.zh: 進樞密都承旨，未受命而卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Chief Secretary of the Privy Council but died before he could accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief secretary of the Privy Council but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 賜對衣、金帶，守龍圖閣待制致仕，特贈四官。

translations.literal: He was granted court robes and a gold belt, kept at the Dragon Diagram Hall as Gentleman Emeritus, and specially posthumously promoted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him robes and a gold belt, allowed him to retire as Gentleman of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and specially promoted him four ranks posthumously.

sentences.zh: 棄疾豪爽尚氣節，識拔英俊，所交多海內知名士。

translations.literal: Qiji was bold and generous and prized integrity; he recognized and promoted outstanding men, and those he befriended were mostly renowned figures within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji was bold and open-handed, valued integrity, spotted and advanced talented men, and most of his friends were celebrated figures across the empire.

sentences.zh: 嘗跋紹興間詔書曰：「使此詔出於紹興之前，可以無事仇之大恥；

translations.literal: He once wrote a colophon to an edict of the Shaoxing period saying: "Had this edict issued before Shaoxing, the great shame of our enemy might have been avoided;
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a colophon on an edict from the Shaoxing era: "Had this edict come before Shaoxing, the great shame of our enemy need never have been borne;

sentences.zh: 使此詔行於隆興之後，可以卒不世之大功。

translations.literal: had this edict been carried out after Longxing, the unexampled great achievement might have been completed.
translations.idiomatic: had it been enforced after Longxing, the unparalleled great achievement might have been finished.

sentences.zh: 今此詔與仇敵俱存也，悲夫！」

translations.literal: Now this edict exists together with the enemy—how sad!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict survives side by side with the enemy—how bitter!"

sentences.zh: 人服其警切。

translations.literal: People admired the sharpness of his words.
translations.idiomatic: Men admired the force of his judgment.

sentences.zh: 帥長沙時，士人或訴考試官濫取第十七名《春秋》卷，棄疾察之信然，索亞榜《春秋》卷兩易之，啟名則趙鼎也。

translations.literal: When he commanded Changsha, a scholar complained that the examination officer had wrongly taken the seventeenth Spring and Autumn examination paper; Qiji investigated and found it true, demanded the secondary list Spring and Autumn papers and exchanged two, and when the name was opened it was Zhao Ding.
translations.idiomatic: While commanding Changsha, a candidate complained that the examiner had wrongly advanced the seventeenth-ranked Spring and Autumn paper; Xin Qiji looked into it, found the charge true, took two papers from the secondary list and swapped them, and when the seal was broken the name was Zhao Ding.

sentences.zh: 棄疾怒曰：「佐國元勳，忠簡一人，胡為又一趙鼎！」

translations.literal: Qiji said in anger: "The founding minister of the state, the loyal and simple man alone—why yet another Zhao Ding!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji flared up: "The state's founding pillar, the one loyal and steadfast minister—and now another Zhao Ding!"

sentences.zh: 擲之地。

translations.literal: He threw it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled the paper to the floor.

sentences.zh: 次閱《禮記》卷，棄疾曰：「觀其議論，必豪傑士也，此不可失。」

translations.literal: Next he reviewed the Book of Rites paper and said: "Judging from the argument, this must be a heroic scholar—this one must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the next Book of Rites paper he said, "From the argument this must be a heroic scholar—we cannot let this one slip."

sentences.zh: 啟之，乃趙方也。

translations.literal: When it was opened it was Zhao Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When the name was opened it was Zhao Fang.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「人生在勤，當以力田為先。

translations.literal: He once said: "Life lies in diligence; one should take strenuous farming as the first thing.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Life depends on diligence; strenuous farming should come first.

sentences.zh: 北方之人，養生之具不求於人，是以無甚富甚貧之家。

translations.literal: People of the north do not seek the means of sustaining life from others; therefore there are no extremely rich or extremely poor households.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners do not look to others for their livelihood, and so you find neither great wealth nor great poverty.

sentences.zh: 南方多末作以病農，而兼併之患興，貧富斯不侔矣。」

translations.literal: The south has many secondary crafts that injure farming, and the affliction of encroachment arises; rich and poor are then no longer equal."
translations.idiomatic: The south piles up crafts that eat away at farming, encroachment flourishes, and rich and poor are no longer matched."

sentences.zh: 故以「稼」名軒。

translations.literal: Therefore he styled his studio "Farming."
translations.idiomatic: That is why he named his studio Farming.

sentences.zh: 為大理卿時，同僚吳交如死，無棺斂，棄疾歎曰：「身為列卿而貧若此，是廉介之士也！」

translations.literal: When he was Director of Justice, his colleague Wu Jiaoru died without a coffin or shroud; Qiji sighed and said: "Though a ranked minister, to be so poor—this is a man of integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Court of Justice, his colleague Wu Jiaoru died without coffin or shroud; Xin Qiji sighed, "A full minister yet so poor—this is a man of integrity!"

sentences.zh: 既厚賻之，復言於執政，詔賜銀絹。

translations.literal: He gave a generous funeral gift and also spoke to the chief ministers; an edict granted silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He gave a generous funeral gift, spoke to the chief ministers, and an edict awarded silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 棄疾嘗同朱熹遊武夷山，賦《九曲棹歌》，熹書「克己復禮」、「夙興夜寐」，題其二齋室。

translations.literal: Qiji once traveled Mount Wuyi with Zhu Xi and composed the "Nine-Bend Oar Song"; Xi wrote "Restrain the self and return to propriety" and "Rise early and sleep late" and inscribed his two studio rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji once toured Mount Wuyi with Zhu Xi, wrote the Nine-Bend Oar Song, and Zhu Xi inscribed his two studios with "Restrain the self and return to propriety" and "Rise early and sleep late."

sentences.zh: 熹歿，偽學禁方嚴，門生故舊至無送葬者。

translations.literal: When Xi died the ban on "false learning" was severe; students and old friends down to none attended the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi died the ban on so-called false learning was at its height; not even students and old friends came to bury him.

sentences.zh: 棄疾為文往哭之曰：「所不朽者，垂萬世名。

translations.literal: Qiji wrote a text to mourn him saying: "What does not perish casts a name for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji wrote a lament: "What never perishes is a name that lasts ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 孰謂公死，凜凜猶生！」

translations.literal: Who says the lord is dead? Stern and bright, he still lives!"
translations.idiomatic: Who says he is gone? Stern and bright, he still lives!"

sentences.zh: 棄疾雅善長短句，悲壯激烈，有《稼軒集》行世。

translations.literal: Qiji was skilled in long and short lyrics, tragic and fierce; the Jiaxuan Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji excelled at ci poetry—fierce and tragic in tone—and his Jiaxuan Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 紹定六年，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoding (1233) he was posthumously granted Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoding (1233) he was posthumously made Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 咸淳閑，史館校勘謝枋得過棄疾墓旁僧舍，有疾聲大呼於堂上，若嗚其不平，自昏暮至三鼓不絕聲。

translations.literal: In the Xianchun period, Palace Revisionist Xie Fangde passed the monk's lodge beside Qiji's tomb; a sick voice cried loudly in the hall as if voicing injustice, from dusk to the third watch without cease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianchun era, palace revisionist Xie Fangde stayed at a monk's lodge by Xin Qiji's tomb; a hoarse voice shouted in the hall as though airing a grievance, from dusk until the third watch without stopping.

sentences.zh: 枋得秉燭作文，旦且祭之，文成而聲始息。

translations.literal: Fangde took up a candle and composed a text; at dawn he sacrificed, and when the text was finished the sound ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde lit a candle and wrote a memorial essay, sacrificed at dawn, and only when the piece was finished did the voice fall silent.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，枋得請於朝，加贈少師，諡忠敏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou (1275) Fangde petitioned court to add the posthumous title Junior Preceptor and give the temple name Loyal and Keen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Deyou (1275) Fangde petitioned the court to add the posthumous rank Junior Preceptor and the temple name Loyal and Keen.

sentences.zh: 何異，字同叔，撫州崇仁人。

translations.literal: He Yi, styled Tongshu, was a man of Chongren in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Yi, whose courtesy name was Tongshu, came from Chongren in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年進士，調石城主簿，曆兩任，知蘋鄉縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing (1154) he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Shicheng, served two terms, and became magistrate of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing (1154), served as registrar of Shicheng through two terms, and became magistrate of Pingxiang County.

sentences.zh: 丞相周必大、參政留正以院轄擬異，孝宗問有無列薦，正等以萍鄉政績對，乃遷國子監主簿。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zhou Bida and Participant Liu Zheng planned to nominate Yi through the Academy; Xiaozong asked whether anyone had jointly recommended him; Zheng answered with Pingxiang administrative achievements, and he was moved to Registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Zhou Bida and participant Liu Zheng meant to nominate him through the Hanlin Academy; Emperor Xiaozong asked whether anyone had jointly recommended him, and Zheng cited his record at Pingxiang, whereupon Yi was made registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 遷丞，轉對，所言帝喜之，曰：「君臣一體，初不在事形跡，有所見聞，于銀台司繳奏。」

translations.literal: He was moved to Assistant Director and presented at court; the emperor was pleased with his words and said: "Ruler and minister are one body; at first it does not lie in the form of things—whatever you see and hear, submit it through the Silver Terrace Office."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to assistant director, he spoke at court; the emperor was pleased and said, "Ruler and minister are one body—the bond is not mere ceremony; report whatever you observe through the Silver Terrace Office."

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 異奏與丞相留正舊同官，不敢供職，禦劄不許引嫌，遂拜命。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized that he had formerly served with Chief Councilor Liu Zheng and dared not take office; an imperial note forbade citing personal ties, and he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized that he had once served alongside Chief Councilor Liu Zheng and could not in conscience take the post; an imperial note forbade pleading personal ties, and he accepted the seal.

sentences.zh: 遷右正言。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 時光宗愆於定省，異入疏諫，不報。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Guangzong was remiss in attending his parents; Yi entered a memorial to remonstrate and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong was then neglecting visits to his parents; Yi submitted a remonstrance and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 約台官聯名，言奸人離間父子，當明正典刑，語極峻，又不報。

translations.literal: He arranged for censors to memorialize jointly that wicked men were estranging father and son and the statutory penalties should be made clear; the language was extremely stern, and again there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged for the censorate to memorialize jointly that villains were driving father and son apart and the law should be enforced in full; the wording was severe, and again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 丐外，授湖南轉運判官。

translations.literal: He begged an outside post and was granted Transport Judge of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the capital and was made transport judge of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 偶攝帥事，辰蠻侵擾邵陽，異募山丁捕首亂者，蒲來矢以眾來降。

translations.literal: He happened to act as commander; Chen tribesmen harassed Shaoyang; Yi recruited hill men to capture the ringleaders, and Pulai Shi came with his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While acting as commander, Chen tribesmen raided Shaoyang; Yi recruited hill tribesmen to seize the ringleaders, and Pulai Shi brought his men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋為浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Soon he became Judicial Intendant of Western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made judicial intendant of Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 乙太常少卿召，改秘書監兼實錄院檢討官，權禮部侍郎、太常寺。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and summoned; he was made Director of the Secretariat while also Revisionist of the Veritable Records and Acting Vice Minister of Rites and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and summoned, he became director of the Secretariat with concurrent duty as revisionist of the Veritable Records and acting vice minister of rites and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太廟芝草生，韓侂胄率百官觀焉，異謂其色白，慮生兵妖，侂胄不悅。

translations.literal: Auspicious fungus grew in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Han Tuozhou led the hundred officials to view it; Yi said its color was white and he feared it foretold military prodigies; Tuozhou was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi fungus appeared in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Han Tuozhou led the officials to view it; Yi said its white color might portend war; Tuozhou took offense.

sentences.zh: 又以劉光祖於異交密，言者遂以異在言路不彈丞相留正及受趙汝愚薦，劾罷之，久乃予祠。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Liu Guangzu was on intimate terms with Yi, critics charged that Yi on the remonstrance path had not impeached Chief Councilor Liu Zheng and had accepted Zhao Ruyu's recommendation; he was impeached and dismissed; only after a long while was he granted a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Guangzu was close to Yi, critics charged that Yi had failed to impeach Liu Zheng while on the remonstrance track and had accepted Zhao Ruyu's patronage; he was impeached and removed, and only long afterward received a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 起知夔州兼本路安撫。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Kuizhou while also pacification commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Kuizhou with concurrent duty as pacification commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 異以夔民土狹食少，同轉運司糴米樁積，立迴圈通濟倉。

translations.literal: Yi said the people of Kuizhou had narrow land and little food; together with the transport commission he bought rice for storage and founded the Revolving Relief Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said the people of Kuizhou had little land and scarce grain; working with the transport commission he bought rice for storage and established the Revolving Relief Granary.

sentences.zh: 七月丙戌，西北有星白芒墜地，其聲如雷，異曰：「戌日酉時，火土交會，而妖星自東南沖西北，化為天狗，蜀其將有兵乎？」

translations.literal: On the seventh month, day bingxu, a star with white rays fell to earth in the northwest with a sound like thunder; Yi said: "On the day xu at the hour you, fire and earth meet, while the prodigious star from the southeast strikes the northwest and becomes the Heavenly Dog—will Shu soon have war?"
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh month, day bingxu, a star with a white tail fell in the northwest with a thunderous roar; Yi said, "On a xu day at the you hour, fire and earth conjoin while an ominous star shoots from the southeast toward the northwest and turns into the Heavenly Dog—will Shu soon see war?"

sentences.zh: 丐祠，以寶謨閣待制提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He begged a temple post and was made Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Planning in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a sinecure and was made Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Planning in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 後四年，吳曦果叛。

translations.literal: Four years later Wu Xi did indeed rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Wu Xi did rebel, just as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 起知潭州，乞閑予祠者再。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Tanzhou and twice begged leisure and was granted temple posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Tanzhou and twice asked to retire and was granted sinecures.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading (1208) he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading (1208) he was summoned as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 五月不雨，異上封事言：「近日號令或從中出，而執政不得與聞其事，台諫不得盡行其言。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rain did not fall; Yi submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Recently orders sometimes issue from within and the chief ministers do not hear of the matter; remonstrators cannot fully carry out their words.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifth month brought no rain, Yi submitted a sealed memorial: "Lately orders sometimes come from the inner palace while the chief ministers never hear of them, and remonstrators cannot fully speak their minds.

sentences.zh: 陛下閔念饑民，藥病殯死，遐荒僻嶠，安得實惠？

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities the starving people, heals the sick and buries the dead—how can remote borderlands receive real benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the starving, tends the sick and buries the dead—how can distant borderlands receive real relief?

sentences.zh: 多方稱提，不如縮造楮幣；

translations.literal: Many schemes to raise the value of paper money are not as good as reducing the manufacture of paper notes;
translations.idiomatic: Many schemes to prop up paper money are not as good as cutting back note issues;

sentences.zh: 阜通商米，不如稍寬關市之征。」

translations.literal: promoting commercial rice is not as good as slightly easing transit-duties at the passes."
translations.idiomatic: flooding the market with grain is not as good as easing tolls at the passes a little."

sentences.zh: 明年，權工部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 告老，抗章言：「近臣求去，類成虛文，中外相觀，指為禮數，無以為風俗廉恥之勸。」

translations.literal: He reported old age and submitted a memorial saying: "Recently close officials who seek to leave mostly turn it into empty form; court and countryside watch each other and treat it as mere ritual, with nothing to encourage integrity and shame in custom."
translations.idiomatic: Reporting his age, he memorialized: "Lately when close officials ask to retire it is mostly empty form; inside and outside the court treat it as ritual only, and nothing remains to encourage integrity in public morals."

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣直學士知泉州，從所乞予祠，進寶章閣學士，轉一官致仕。

translations.literal: He was made Academician of the Hall of Treasured Insignia and prefect of Quanzhou; following his request he was granted a temple post, advanced to Academician of the Hall of Treasured Insignia, and retired with one rank promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall of Treasured Insignia and prefect of Quanzhou; at his request he received a sinecure, was advanced to academician of that hall, and retired with one rank added.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 異高自標緻，有詩名，所著《月湖詩集》行世。

translations.literal: Yi held himself to a high standard and had a name in poetry; his Moon Lake Poetry Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yi set a high standard for himself and was known as a poet; his Moon Lake Poetry Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 授泰興令，有殺人獄具，謂：「禱于叢祠，以殺一人，刃忽三躍，乃殺三人，是神實教我也。」

translations.literal: When appointed magistrate of Taixing, a murder case was complete; the man said: "I prayed at a grove shrine to kill one man; the blade suddenly leaped three times and I killed three—truly the spirit taught me."
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Taixing he had a murder case ready for judgment; the killer said, "I prayed at a roadside shrine to kill one man; the blade leapt three times and I killed three—the god truly commanded me."

sentences.zh: 為請之州，毀其廟，斬首以徇。

translations.literal: He petitioned the prefecture, destroyed the shrine, and beheaded the man as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the prefecture, tore down the shrine, and beheaded the killer as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有租牛縣境者，租戶于主有連姻，因喪會，竊券而逃。

translations.literal: In a neighboring county an ox was rented within the county border; the tenant was related by marriage to the owner; at a funeral gathering he stole the contract and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In a neighboring county an ox was hired out within Taixing's border; the tenant was related by marriage to the owner and, at a funeral feast, stole the lease and fled.

sentences.zh: 它日主之子征其租，則曰牛鬻久矣。

translations.literal: Later the owner's son collected rent and was told the ox had long been sold.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the owner's son came to collect rent and was told the ox had been sold long ago.

sentences.zh: 子累年訟於官，無券可質，官又以異縣置不問。

translations.literal: The son sued at court for years; with no contract to prove his claim, officials also set it aside because it was another county.
translations.idiomatic: The son sued for years; without the contract he could not prove his case, and officials ignored it because the matter lay in another county.

sentences.zh: 至是訴於宰，宰曰：「牛失十載，安得一旦復之。」

translations.literal: He now appealed to the magistrate, who said: "The ox has been lost ten years—how can it be recovered in a day?"
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to Liu Zai, who said, "The ox has been gone ten years—how can we recover it overnight?"

sentences.zh: 乃召二丐者勞而語之故，托以它事系獄，鞫之，丐者自詭盜牛以賣，遣詣其所驗視。

translations.literal: He summoned two beggars, treated them kindly and told them the story, detained them on another charge, interrogated them, and the beggars themselves confessed to stealing and selling the ox; he sent them to identify the place.
translations.idiomatic: He called in two beggars, treated them well and explained the case, jailed them on another pretext, questioned them, and they confessed to stealing and selling the ox; he sent them to point out the spot.

sentences.zh: 租戶曰：「吾牛因某氏所租。

translations.literal: The tenant said: "My ox was rented to a certain family.
translations.idiomatic: The tenant said, "My ox was hired out to such-and-such a household.

sentences.zh: 丐者辭益力，因出券示之，相持以來，盜券者憮然，為歸牛與租。

translations.literal: The beggars argued all the more; he produced the contract; they came in dispute; the thief who had stolen the contract was dismayed and returned the ox and rent.
translations.idiomatic: The beggars protested harder until he produced the contract; they came back arguing; the man who had stolen the lease was stunned and returned ox and rent.

sentences.zh: 富室亡金釵，惟二僕婦在，置之有司，鹹以為冤。

translations.literal: A rich household lost a gold hairpin; only two maidservants were present; they were handed to the authorities and all thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy family lost a gold hairpin with only two maidservants at home; both were handed to the magistrate, and everyone thought them wronged.

sentences.zh: 命各持一蘆，曰：「非盜釵者，詰朝蘆當自若；

translations.literal: He ordered each to hold a reed and said: "If you did not steal the hairpin, tomorrow the reed will be as before;"
translations.idiomatic: He had each hold a reed and said, "If you did not steal the pin, your reed will be unchanged tomorrow;

sentences.zh: 果盜，則長於今二寸。」

translations.literal: if you did steal it, it will be two inches longer than today."
translations.idiomatic: "if you did steal it, it will be two inches longer than today."

sentences.zh: 明旦視之，一自若，一去其蘆二寸矣，即訊之，果伏其罪。

translations.literal: At dawn one was as before and one had lost two inches from the reed; he questioned her and she indeed confessed the crime.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn one reed was unchanged and the other was two inches shorter; he questioned the maid and she confessed.

sentences.zh: 有姑訴婦不養者二，召二婦並姑置一室，或餉其婦而不及姑，徐伺之，一婦每以己饌饋姑，姑猶呵之，其一反之。

translations.literal: Two mothers-in-law each sued that their daughters-in-law did not support them; he summoned both daughters-in-law and mothers-in-law to one room; sometimes food was given to the daughter-in-law but not the mother-in-law; he watched quietly—one daughter-in-law always shared her own food with her mother-in-law though the mother-in-law still scolded her, while the other did the opposite.
translations.idiomatic: Two mothers-in-law sued their daughters-in-law for neglect; he put both pairs in one room; sometimes food reached the daughter-in-law but not the mother-in-law; watching quietly, he saw one daughter-in-law always shared her portion though the mother-in-law scolded her, while the other did the reverse.

sentences.zh: 如是累日，遂得其情。

translations.literal: After several days in this way he obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he learned the truth.

sentences.zh: 父喪，免，至京，韓侂胄方謀用兵，宰啟鄧友龍、薛叔似極言輕挑兵端，為國深害，迄如其言。

translations.literal: When his father died he left office; reaching the capital, Han Tuozhou was plotting war; Zai reported to the chief minister that Deng Youlong and Xue Shusi were extremely reckless in provoking military action and deeply harmful to the state—events turned out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he left office; in the capital Han Tuozhou was plotting war; Liu Zai told the chief minister that Deng Youlong and Xue Shusi were rashly provoking hostilities and would deeply harm the state—and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 為浙東倉司幹官，職事修舉，亟引去，默觀時變，頓不樂仕。

translations.literal: As planning officer of the Eastern Zhe Granary Commission he performed his duties well but quickly withdrew, silently watching the times and suddenly disliking office.
translations.idiomatic: As planning officer on the Eastern Zhe Granary Commission he did his work well but soon withdrew, watching the times in silence and losing all taste for office.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，監南嶽廟。

translations.literal: Soon he reported home and supervised the Southern Sacred Mountain Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return home and took charge of the Southern Sacred Mountain Temple.

sentences.zh: 江、淮制置使黃度辟之入幕，宰辭曰：「君命召不往，今矧可出耶？」

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai Pacification Commissioner Huang Du invited him into his staff; Zai declined, saying: "When the ruler summons I do not go—how much less now?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner Huang Du invited him into his staff; Liu Zai declined: "When the ruler summoned I did not go—how could I go now?"

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年，堂審召命且再下，不至。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading (1211) the court review summons came down twice more and he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiading (1211) the court review summons came twice more and he still did not come.

sentences.zh: 時相亦屢諷執政、從官貽書挽宰，宰峻辭以絕。

translations.literal: The chief minister also several times hinted to administrators and attendants to send letters urging Zai; Zai sternly refused to end it.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister also repeatedly hinted to administrators and attendants to write and urge him; Liu Zai flatly refused.

sentences.zh: 俄題考功曆，示決不復仕。

translations.literal: Soon he entered his merit review register, showing he would never serve again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered his merit review register, making clear he would never serve again.

sentences.zh: 理宗初即位，以為籍田令，屢辭，改添差通判建康府，又辭，乞致仕，乃以直秘閣主管仙都觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong first took the throne he was made Director of the Altar Fields; he declined repeatedly, was changed to additional Vice Prefect of Jiankang, declined again, begged to retire, and was made Gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of the Xiandu Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong first ascended the throne Liu Zai was made director of the altar fields; he declined repeatedly, was offered additional vice prefect of Jiankang and declined again, asked to retire, and was made gentleman of the Secretariat in charge of the Xiandu Abbey.

sentences.zh: 拜改秩予祠之命，辭秘閣，不允。

translations.literal: He received orders for rank change and a temple post and declined the Secretariat post; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He received orders promoting his rank and granting a sinecure and declined the Secretariat post; the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，升直寶謨閣，祠如故，且盡還磨勘歲月。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping (1234) he was advanced to Gentleman of the Direct Hall of Treasured Planning with the same temple duty, and all withheld merit-review years were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping (1234) he was advanced to gentleman of the Direct Hall of Treasured Planning with the same sinecure, and all withheld merit-review years were restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷太常丞，郡守以朝命趣行，不得已勉就道，至吳門，拜疏徑歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the prefect urged him by court order; he had no choice but to set out reluctantly; reaching Wu Gate he memorialized and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the prefect pressed him with court orders; he reluctantly set out, reached Wu Gate, memorialized, and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 一時譽望，收召略盡，所不能致者，宰與崔與之耳。

translations.literal: At that time men of reputation were recalled almost entirely; those who could not be brought in were Zai and Cui Yuzhi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Men of reputation were then recalled almost without exception; those who could not be persuaded were Liu Zai and Cui Yuzhi alone.

sentences.zh: 帝側席以問侍御史王遂，且俾宣撫。

translations.literal: The emperor leaned forward in his seat to ask Attending Censor Wang Sui and also ordered him to announce and comfort Zai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned forward to ask attending censor Wang Sui and also ordered him to announce the summons and comfort Liu Zai.

sentences.zh: 遷將作少監，又以直敷文閣知甯國府，皆不拜。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of Palace Construction and again offered Direct Hall of Spreading Culture and prefect of Ningguo—all declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of palace construction and again offered gentleman of the Direct Hall of Spreading Culture and prefect of Ningguo—all declined.

sentences.zh: 進直顯謨閣、主管玉局觀，帝猶冀宰一來也。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Gentleman of the Direct Hall of Manifest Planning in charge of the Jade Bureau Abbey; the emperor still hoped Zai would come once.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to gentleman of the Direct Hall of Manifest Planning in charge of the Jade Bureau Abbey; the emperor still hoped Liu Zai would come once.

sentences.zh: 召奏事，訖不為起。

translations.literal: Summoned to report at court, in the end he would not rise to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to report at court, he still would not take office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，鄉人罷市走送，袂相屬者五十里，人人如哭其私親。

translations.literal: Soon he died; fellow townsmen closed markets and ran to send him off; sleeves linked for fifty li; each person mourned as for a close kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; townspeople closed their shops and ran to escort him, sleeves linked for fifty li, each mourning as for a kinsman.

sentences.zh: 宰剛大正直，明敏仁恕，施惠鄉邦，其烈實多。

translations.literal: Zai was upright, great, bright, perceptive, benevolent, and forgiving; he bestowed favors on his native district and his achievements were many.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zai was upright, forthright, bright, perceptive, benevolent, and forgiving; he showered benefits on his home district and his deeds were many.

sentences.zh: 置義倉，創義役，三為粥以與餓者，自冬徂夏，日食凡萬餘人，薪粟、衣纊、藥餌、棺衾之類，靡謁不獲。

translations.literal: He established a charity granary, created voluntary corvée service, three times set out gruel for the hungry; from winter to summer more than ten thousand ate daily; fuel, grain, clothing, medicine, coffins, and shrouds—none who asked went away empty.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a charity granary and voluntary labor service, three times gave gruel to the hungry—from winter through summer more than ten thousand people ate daily—and for fuel, grain, clothing, medicine, coffins, and shrouds, none who asked left empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 某無田可耕，某無廬可居，某之子女長矣而未昏嫁，皆汲汲經理，如己實任其責。

translations.literal: If someone had no fields to till, no house to dwell in, or children grown yet unmarried, he hurried to arrange it as though he truly bore the responsibility himself.
translations.idiomatic: If someone lacked land to farm, a roof to live under, or grown children still unmarried, he hurried to arrange it as though the duty were his own.

sentences.zh: 橋有病涉，路有險阻，雖巨役必捐貲先倡而程其事。

translations.literal: Where bridges made crossing difficult or roads were perilous, even great projects he would donate funds first and oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Where bridges made crossing hard or roads were dangerous, even for great works he donated first and supervised the job.

sentences.zh: 宰生理素薄，見義必為，既竭其力，藉質貸以繼之無倦。

translations.literal: Zai's means were always thin, but seeing justice he must act; when he had exhausted his strength he borrowed on pledge and continued without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: His means were always modest, yet whenever he saw a just cause he acted; when his strength was spent he borrowed on pledge and kept going without tiring.

sentences.zh: 若定折麥錢額，更縣鬥斛如制，毀淫祠八十四所，凡可以白於有司、利於鄉人者，無不為也。

translations.literal: He fixed wheat-money quotas, restored county measures to the standard, destroyed eighty-four illicit shrines—whatever could be reported to officials for the benefit of the district, he did it.
translations.idiomatic: He set fair wheat-money quotas, restored county measures to standard, tore down eighty-four illicit shrines—whatever could be reported to officials for the people's good, he did.

sentences.zh: 宰隱居三十年，平生無嗜好，惟書靡所不讀。

translations.literal: Zai lived in seclusion thirty years; in life he had no hobby except that he read every book.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zai lived in retirement thirty years; he had no hobby in life except reading every book he could.

sentences.zh: 既竭日力，猶坐以待，雖博考訓注，而自得之為貴。

translations.literal: When he had exhausted the day's strength he still sat waiting; though he broadly examined glosses and commentaries, what he grasped for himself was what he prized.
translations.idiomatic: Even after exhausting the daylight he sat on in study; though he read widely in commentaries, what he understood for himself was what he valued.

sentences.zh: 有《漫塘文集》、《語錄》行世。

translations.literal: His Random Pond Collected Writings and Recorded Sayings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Random Pond Collected Writings and Recorded Sayings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉爚，字晦伯，建陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Yue, styled Huibo, was a man of Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue, whose courtesy name was Huibo, came from Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 與弟韜仲受學于朱熹、呂祖謙。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Tao Zhong he received learning from Zhu Xi and Lü Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Tao Zhong studied under Zhu Xi and Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年舉進士，調山陰主簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao (1172) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qiandao (1172) he passed the jinshi examination and was made registrar of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 爚正版籍，吏不容奸。

translations.literal: Yue rectified the household registers and clerks could not practice fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue straightened the household registers so clerks could not cheat.

sentences.zh: 調饒州錄事，通判黃奕將以事汙爚，而己自以贓抵罪去。

translations.literal: Transferred to Recorder of Raozhou, Vice Prefect Huang Yi was about to defile Yue with a charge when he himself was convicted of bribery and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to recorder of Raozhou, Vice Prefect Huang Yi meant to frame Liu Yue with a charge but was himself convicted of bribery and left office.

sentences.zh: 都大坑冶耿某閔遺骸暴露，議用浮屠法葬之水火，爚貽書曰：「使死者有知，禍亦慘矣。」

translations.literal: Director-General of Mining Geng someone pitied exposed remains and proposed burying them by Buddhist cremation; Yue sent a letter saying: "If the dead had consciousness, the harm would also be cruel."
translations.idiomatic: The director-general of mining, Master Geng, pitied exposed corpses and proposed Buddhist cremation; Liu Yue wrote, "If the dead had awareness, the harm would be cruel indeed."

sentences.zh: 請擇高阜為叢塚以葬。

translations.literal: He asked to choose a high mound for a communal burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a high mound be chosen for a communal burial ground.

sentences.zh: 調蓮城令，罷添給錢及綱運例錢，免上供銀錢及綱本、二稅甲葉、鈔鹽、軍期米等錢，大修學校，乞行經界。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Liancheng, he abolished supplemental pay and routine transport fees, exempted tribute silver and notes for transport principal, second tax registration leaves, salt coupons, and garrison-period rice, greatly repaired schools, and petitioned to carry out the field-boundary system.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Liancheng he abolished supplemental pay and routine transport fees, exempted tribute silver, transport principal, second-tax registration fees, salt coupons, and garrison rice money, greatly repaired the schools, and petitioned to implement the field-boundary system.

sentences.zh: 改知閩縣，治以清簡，庭無滯訟，興利去害，知無不為。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Min County; his rule was pure and simple; no cases stagnated in court; he promoted benefit and removed harm wherever he knew how.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Min County; his administration was pure and spare; no suit lingered in court; he advanced public good and removed harm wherever he could.

sentences.zh: 差通判潭州，未上，丁父憂。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Prefect of Tanzhou but had not reported when his father died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice prefect of Tanzhou but had not taken up the post when his father died.

sentences.zh: 偽學禁興，爚從熹武夷山講道讀書，怡然自適。

translations.literal: When the ban on false learning arose, Yue followed Xi to lecture and read on Mount Wuyi, content and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the ban on so-called false learning arose, Liu Yue followed Zhu Xi to study on Mount Wuyi, content and at ease.

sentences.zh: 築雲莊山房，為終老隱居之計。

translations.literal: He built the Cloud Studio mountain retreat as his plan for final retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Cloud Studio mountain retreat as his plan to end his days in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 調贛州坑冶司主管文字，差知德慶府，大修學校，奏便民五事，又奏罷兩縣無名租錢，糾集武勇民兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed clerk of the Ganzhou Mining Office, then made prefect of Deqing, greatly repaired schools, memorialized five measures for the people's benefit, memorialized to abolish nameless rents in two counties, and mustered martial militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was made clerk of the Ganzhou Mining Office, then prefect of Deqing; he greatly repaired schools, memorialized five measures for the people's benefit, petitioned to abolish unnamed levies in two counties, and mustered martial militia.

sentences.zh: 入奏言：「前者北伐之役，執事者不度事勢，貽陛下憂。

translations.literal: Entering court to report he said: "The former northern expedition—those in charge did not measure the situation and brought worry on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting at court he said, "In the last northern campaign those in charge misread the situation and brought Your Majesty grief.

sentences.zh: 今雖從和議，願益恐懼修省，必開言路以廣忠益，必張公道以進人才，必飭邊備以防敵患。」

translations.literal: Now though we follow the peace agreement, I wish Your Majesty would all the more fear, reflect, and mend, must open the path of speech to broaden loyal benefit, must expand public justice to advance talent, and must tighten border defense to guard against enemy trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Though we now keep the peace treaty, I beg Your Majesty to fear all the more, reflect, and mend—to open channels of loyal counsel, to uphold public justice and advance talent, and to tighten border defenses against the enemy."

sentences.zh: 提舉廣東常平。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of Guangdong Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of Guangdong Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 令守臣歲以一半易新，春末支，及冬復償，存其半以備緩急。

translations.literal: He ordered guarding officials each year to exchange half for new grain, disburse at late spring, repay by winter, and keep half in reserve for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered local officials each year to replace half the stock with new grain, issue it in late spring, repay by winter, and keep half in reserve for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 逋欠亭戶錢十萬，轉運司五萬，爚以公使，公用二庫贏錢補之。

translations.literal: Ten thousand in arrears from saltern households and fifty thousand from the transport commission—Yue made up the sums from public envoys and the surplus of the two public treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears of ten thousand from saltern households and fifty thousand from the transport commission—Liu Yue covered them from public envoys' funds and surpluses in the two public treasuries.

sentences.zh: 奏議倉之敝、客丁錢之敝、小官奉給之敝、舉留守令之敝、吏商之敝。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the abuses of the deliberation granary, guest labor money, petty officials' salaries, recommending acting prefects and magistrates, and clerk-merchants.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on abuses in the deliberation granary, guest labor fees, petty officials' salaries, recommending acting prefects and magistrates, and clerk-merchants.

sentences.zh: 召入奏事，首論：「公道明，則人心自一，朝廷自尊，雖危可安也；

translations.literal: Summoned to report at court, he first discussed: "When public justice is clear, then hearts are of themselves one, the court is of itself honored, and though in peril it can be safe;
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he began: "When public justice is clear, hearts unite of themselves, the court stands honored of itself, and even in danger the state can be safe;

sentences.zh: 公道廢，則人心自貳，朝廷自輕，雖安易危也。」

translations.literal: when public justice is abandoned, then hearts are of themselves divided, the court is of itself slighted, and though at peace it is easy to fall into peril."
translations.idiomatic: when public justice is abandoned, hearts divide of themselves, the court grows light of itself, and even in peace peril comes easily."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉獎。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 遷尚左郎官，請節內外冗費以收楮幣。

translations.literal: He was moved to Left Director in the Ministry of Revenue and asked to cut redundant expenses inside and outside to recover paper money.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left director in the Ministry of Revenue and asked to trim redundant spending throughout the government to shore up paper currency.

sentences.zh: 轉對言：「願於經筵講讀、大臣奏對，反復問難，以求義理之當否，與政事之得失，則聖學進而治道隆矣。」

translations.literal: Presenting at court he said: "I wish that in lecture and reading at the classics mat and in chief ministers' memorial replies, questions and challenges be repeated back and forth to seek whether principles are right or wrong and whether administration gains or loses—then sagely learning will advance and the way of governance will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: At court he said, "I wish that at the classics mat and in ministers' replies the emperor would press back and forth on right and wrong in principle and gain and loss in policy—then royal learning would deepen and governance would rise."

sentences.zh: 乞收拾人才及修明軍政。

translations.literal: He begged to gather talent and to clarify military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to gather talent and restore military administration.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提點刑獄，巡按不避寒暑，多所平反。

translations.literal: He was moved to Judicial Intendant of Western Zhe; on inspection tours he did not avoid cold or heat and reversed many wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Made judicial intendant of Western Zhe, he toured without shirking heat or cold and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 有殺人而匿權家者，吏弗敢捕，爚竟獲之。

translations.literal: There were killers sheltered by powerful families whom clerks dared not arrest; Yue ultimately captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Some killers were hidden by powerful families and clerks dared not seize them; Liu Yue still took them in the end.

sentences.zh: 遷國子司業，言于丞相史彌遠，請以熹所著《論語》、《中庸》、《大學》、《孟子》之說以備勸講，正君定國，慰天下學士大夫之心。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and spoke to Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan, asking that Xi's expositions of the Analects, Doctrine of the Mean, Great Learning, and Mencius be used to prepare lectures, stabilize the ruler and state, and comfort the hearts of scholars throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education, he told Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan to use Zhu Xi's commentaries on the Four Books for imperial lectures—to steady ruler and state and hearten scholars everywhere.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「宋興，《六經》微旨，孔、孟遺言，發明於千載之後，以事父則孝，以事君則忠，而世之所謂道學也。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Since Song arose, the subtle purport of the Six Classics and the legacy words of Confucius and Mencius have been brought forth after a thousand years—to serve the father is filial, to serve the ruler is loyal—and this is what the world calls the Learning of the Way.
