translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Since the Song rose, the deep meaning of the Six Classics and the teachings of Confucius and Mencius have been renewed after a thousand years—filial in serving father, loyal in serving ruler—and this is what men call the Learning of the Way.

sentences.zh: 慶元以來，權佞當國，惡人議己，指道為偽，屏其人，禁其書，學者無所依鄉，義利不明，趨向汙下，人欲橫流，廉恥日喪。

translations.literal: Since Qingyuan, powerful sycophants have held the state, hated those who discussed them, called the Way false, barred its people, and banned its books; scholars had nowhere to turn, right and profit were unclear, trends sank low, human desire flooded, and integrity daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qingyuan, powerful sycophants have ruled, hated criticism, called the Way false learning, barred its followers and banned its books; scholars lost their footing, profit eclipsed principle, desire ran wild, and shame daily faded.

sentences.zh: 追惟前日禁絕道學之事，不得不任其咎。

translations.literal: Looking back on the former day's ban on the Learning of the Way, one must bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on the ban on the Learning of the Way, one cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 望其既仕之後，職業修，名節立，不可得也。

translations.literal: To hope that after they take office their duties are cultivated and their integrity established is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To expect that once in office they will cultivate duty and uphold integrity is impossible.

sentences.zh: 乞罷偽學之詔，息邪說，正人心，宗社之福。」

translations.literal: I beg to abolish the edict on false learning, still heterodox doctrines, rectify human hearts—blessing for altar and state."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to revoke the edict on false learning, silence heterodox talk, and rectify hearts—for the blessing of dynasty and state."

sentences.zh: 又請以熹《白鹿洞規》頒示太學，取熹《四書集注》刊行之。

translations.literal: He also asked that Xi's White Deer Grotto Regulations be promulgated at the Imperial University and Xi's Collected Commentaries on the Four Books be printed.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to promulgate Zhu Xi's White Deer Grotto Regulations at the Imperial University and print his Collected Commentaries on the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 又言：「浙西根本之地，宜詔長吏、監司禁戢強暴，撫柔善良，務儲積以備凶荒，禁科斂以紓民力。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Western Zhe is the root land; I wish an edict to long officials and supervisory commissioners to restrain the violent, soothe the good, store grain against famine, and forbid exactions to ease the people's burden."
translations.idiomatic: He also said Western Zhe was the empire's root and asked an edict for prefects and commissioners to curb violence, soothe the good, stock grain against famine, and forbid exactions to ease the people.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、寶錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Compiler of the National History Office and Revisionist of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as compiler of the National History and revisionist of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 接伴金使於盱眙軍。

translations.literal: He received the Jin envoy at Xuyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Jin envoy at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 還，言：「兩淮之地，藩蔽江南，干戈盜賊之後，宜加經理，必于招集流散之中，就為足食足兵之計。

translations.literal: On return he said: "The lands of the Two Huai screen Jiangnan; after war and banditry they should be better governed; amid gathering the displaced one must make plans for full food and full troops.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he said the Two Huai screened the south; after war and banditry they needed better governance, and amid resettling refugees plans for full granaries and full ranks were essential.

sentences.zh: 臣觀淮東，其地平博膏腴，有陂澤水泉之利，而荒蕪實多。

translations.literal: I observe Huai East: its land is broad, rich, and has the benefit of marshes and springs, yet much lies waste.
translations.idiomatic: Huai East, he said, was broad and fertile with marshes and springs, yet much land lay waste.

sentences.zh: 其民勁悍勇敢，習邊鄙戰鬥之事，而安集者少。

translations.literal: Its people are sturdy, brave, and practiced in border fighting, yet few are settled.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were sturdy and skilled in border war, yet few were settled.

sentences.zh: 誠能經畫郊野，招集散亡，約頃畝以授田，使毋廣占拋荒之患，列溝洫以儲水，且備戎馬馳突之虞。

translations.literal: If one could plan the countryside, gather the scattered, assign fields by acreage so they do not broadly occupy and leave land waste, lay ditches to store water, and also guard against enemy horses charging—
translations.idiomatic: If the countryside were planned, refugees gathered, fields assigned by acre so none lay waste, ditches dug to hold water, and defenses made against enemy cavalry—

sentences.zh: 為之具田器，貸種糧，相其險易，聚為室廬，使相保護，聯以什伍，教以擊刺，使相糾率。

translations.literal: provide farm tools, lend seed grain, gauge terrain, cluster dwellings for mutual protection, link them in tens and fives, teach thrust and cut, and have them lead one another—
translations.idiomatic: if tools and seed were lent, settlements clustered for mutual guard, households grouped in tens and fives, and drill taught so they could lead one another—

sentences.zh: 或鄉為一圍，裏為一隊，建其長，立其副。

translations.literal: perhaps by hamlet as one ring and by village as one squad, establish heads and deputies.
translations.idiomatic: hamlets might form rings and villages squads, each with head and deputy.

sentences.zh: 平居則耕，有警則守，有餘力則戰。」

translations.literal: In peace they plow; in alarm they guard; with spare strength they fight."
translations.idiomatic: In peace they would farm; in alarm defend; with spare strength fight.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 進國子祭酒兼侍立修注官。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Director of the Directorate of Education while also Attending Lecturer and Revisionist.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent duty as attending lecturer and revisionist.

sentences.zh: 論貢舉五敝。

translations.literal: He discussed five abuses of the tribute examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed five abuses in the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 兼權兵部侍郎，改兼權刑部侍郎，封建陽縣開國男，賜食邑。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Acting Vice Minister of War, then Acting Vice Minister of Justice, was enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiyang in Jianyang County, and granted a fief for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of war, then of justice, was enfeoffed Baron of Kaiyang in Jianyang County, and granted a sustenance fief.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎兼國子祭酒，兼太子左諭德，升同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Justice while also Director of the Directorate of Education and Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he was advanced to Joint Compiler of the National History and Joint Revisionist of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice minister of justice he also directed the Directorate of Education and tutored the heir apparent; he was advanced to joint compiler of the National History and joint revisionist of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣爭務容默，有論事稍切者，眾輒指以為異。

translations.literal: At that time court ministers competed in silence; whoever discussed affairs a little sharply was pointed at as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers then vied in silence; whoever spoke sharply was marked as odd.

sentences.zh: 爚奏：「願明詔大臣，崇獎忠讜以作士氣，深戒諛佞以肅具僚。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized: "I wish an edict to great ministers to honor loyal remonstrance and raise morale, and deeply warn against flattery to discipline the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue memorialized: "I wish an edict honoring loyal speech to lift morale and sternly warning against flattery to discipline officials.

sentences.zh: 乞擇州縣獄官。」

translations.literal: He begged to select prison officials of prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to choose prison officials for prefectures and counties."

sentences.zh: 冬雷，上恐懼，爚奏：「遴選監司以考察貪吏為先，訪求民瘼，有澤未下流、令未便民者，悉以實上，變而通之，則民心悅而天意解矣。」

translations.literal: Winter thunder frightened the emperor; Yue memorialized: "Select supervisory commissioners first to investigate greedy officials, seek the people's afflictions, report where favor has not flowed down or orders have not benefited the people in truth, and change to reach them—then hearts will be pleased and heaven's mind resolved."
translations.idiomatic: When winter thunder frightened the court, Liu Yue memorialized: "Choose commissioners to investigate greedy officials, report every hardship the people still suffer, and reform what fails them—then hearts will ease and heaven's anger lift."

sentences.zh: 又請擇沿邊諸將。

translations.literal: He also asked to select generals along the border.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to choose border generals.

sentences.zh: 兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 奏「乞使沿邊之民，各自什伍，教閱於鄉，有急則相救援，無事則耕稼自若，軍政隱然寓於田裏之間，此非止一時之利也。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I beg that border people be grouped in tens and fives, drilled in the hamlets; in emergency they rescue one another, in peace they farm as usual—military government hidden in the fields, benefit not for one season alone."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Let border people group in tens and fives and drill in their hamlets; in crisis let them rescue one another, in peace farm as usual—military order hidden in the fields, a gain not for one season only."

sentences.zh: 請城沿邊州郡、罷遣賀正使。

translations.literal: He asked to fortify border prefectures and commanderies and dismiss envoys congratulating the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to fortify border prefectures and stop New Year congratulation envoys.

sentences.zh: 試刑部侍郎，兼職依舊，賜對衣、金帶，辭，不允。

translations.literal: He was tested for Vice Minister of Justice with duties unchanged, granted court robes and a gold belt, declined, and was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Examined for vice minister of justice with duties unchanged, he was granted court robes and a gold belt, declined, and was refused.

sentences.zh: 兩請致仕，不允。

translations.literal: Twice he asked to retire and was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he asked to retire and was refused.

sentences.zh: 奏絕金人歲幣，建制置司于曆陽以援兩淮。

translations.literal: He memorialized to end the Jin annual tribute and establish a command at Liyang to support the Two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to end the Jin annual tribute and establish a command at Liyang to support the Two Huai.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，應詔上封事，曰：「言語方壅而導之使言，人心方鬱而疏之使通，上既開不諱之門，下必有盡言之士，指陳政事之闕失，明言朝廷之是非。

translations.literal: In summer drought he responded to an edict with a sealed memorial saying: "Speech is just blocked yet you guide it to speak; hearts are just depressed yet you open them to flow—above you have opened the gate of no taboo, below there must be men who speak fully, pointing out administrative faults and stating clearly court right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer drought he submitted a sealed memorial: "Speech is blocked yet you urge men to speak; hearts are pent yet you open them—having opened the gate of no taboo above, below men must speak fully on administrative faults and court right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 或者以為好名要譽，而陛下聽之，則苦言之藥，至言之實，陛下棄之而不恤矣，甘言之疾，華言之腴，陛下受之而不覺矣。」

translations.literal: Some may think it is seeking fame and praise, yet if Your Majesty listens, then the medicine of bitter words and the substance of utmost words—Your Majesty discards and does not pity; the ailment of sweet words, the richness of florid words—Your Majesty receives and does not perceive."
translations.idiomatic: Some may be called fame-seekers, yet if Your Majesty heeds them, bitter truth is medicine you may cast aside; sweet flattery is poison you may swallow unaware."

sentences.zh: 氣罷瑞慶聖節，謝絕金使。

translations.literal: He was indignant and stopped the Auspicious Celebration of the Sagely Birthday and declined the Jin envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, he stopped the Auspicious Celebration of the Sagely Birthday and declined the Jin envoy.

sentences.zh: 進封子爵。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 權工部尚書，賜衣帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Works; he was granted robes, belt, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: As acting minister of works he received robes, belt, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 兼太子右庶子，仍兼左諭德。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Right Vice Tutor of the Heir Apparent while still Left Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as right vice tutor of the heir apparent while remaining left tutor.

sentences.zh: 每講讀至經史所陳聲色嗜欲之戒，輒懇切再三敷陳之。

translations.literal: Whenever lecture reached classical warnings on sound, color, and desire in history, he earnestly set them forth again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever lectures touched classical warnings on pleasure and desire, he pressed them earnestly again and again.

sentences.zh: 進讀《詩》之說，詹事戴溪讀之為之吐舌。

translations.literal: Advancing a lecture on the Odes, Tutor Dai Xi stuck out his tongue at it.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on the Odes, he made Tutor Dai Xi stick out his tongue in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫，官其後，賜諡文簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Grandee of Splendid Happiness, office given to his descendants, posthumous title Literary and Simple bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He died; was posthumously made Grandee of Splendid Happiness, offices granted his heirs, and given the posthumous title Literary and Simple.

sentences.zh: 所著有《奏議》、《史稿》、《經筵故事》、《東宮詩解》、《禮記解》、《講堂故事》、《雲莊外稿》。

translations.literal: His works include Memorials, Historical Drafts, Classics Mat Precedents, Eastern Palace Poetry Exegesis, Rites Exegesis, Lecture Hall Precedents, and Cloud Studio Supplement.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Memorials, Historical Drafts, Classics Mat Precedents, Eastern Palace Poetry Exegesis, Rites Exegesis, Lecture Hall Precedents, and Cloud Studio Supplement.

sentences.zh: 柴中行

translations.literal: Chai Zhongxing
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zhongxing

sentences.zh: 柴中行，字與之，餘幹人。

translations.literal: Chai Zhongxing, styled Yuzhi, was a man of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zhongxing, whose courtesy name was Yuzhi, came from Yugan.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年進士，授撫州軍事推官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi (1190) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed military judge of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi (1190) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed military judge of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 權臣韓侂胄禁道學，校文，轉運司移檄，令自言非偽學，中行奮筆曰：「自幼讀程頤書以收科第，如以為偽，不願考校。」

translations.literal: Powerful minister Han Tuozhou banned the Learning of the Way; in examining essays the transport commission sent a dispatch ordering self-declaration of non-false learning; Zhongxing wrote boldly: "From youth I read Cheng Yi's books to gain rank; if that is false, I do not wish to be examined."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou banned the Learning of the Way, the transport commission ordered candidates to declare they were not false scholars; Chai wrote boldly, "I have read Cheng Yi since youth to pass examinations; if that is false learning, I want no part in the exam."

sentences.zh: 調江州學教授，母喪，免，廣西轉運司辟為幹官，帥將薦之，使其客嘗中行，中行正色曰：「身為大帥，而稱人為恩王、恩相，心竊恥之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Instructor at Jiangzhou School; when his mother died he left office; the Guangxi transport commission recruited him as planning officer; the commander meant to recommend him and had a guest test Zhongxing; Zhongxing said sternly: "As great commander you call people benefactor-lord and benefactor-minister—I am secretly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to instructor at Jiangzhou school, he left office when his mother died; Guangxi transport recruited him as planner; the commander meant to recommend him and sent a guest to sound him out; Chai said sternly, "As commander you call men benefactor-lord and benefactor-minister—I am ashamed.

sentences.zh: 毋汙我！」

translations.literal: Do not defile me!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not stain me!"

sentences.zh: 攝昭州郡事，蠲丁錢，減苗斛，賑饑羸。

translations.literal: Acting prefectural affairs of Zhaozhou, he remitted labor-service money, reduced grain quotas, and relieved the hungry and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Acting for Zhaozhou, he remitted labor money, cut grain quotas, and fed the hungry and weak.

sentences.zh: 轉運司委中行代行部，由桂林屬邑曆柳、象、賓入邕管，問民疾苦，先行而後聞，捐鹽息以惠遠民。

translations.literal: The transport commission entrusted Zhongxing to act in its place; from Guilin through the subordinate counties he passed Liu, Xiang, and Bin into Yong Administration, inquired into the people's hardships, acted first and reported later, and donated salt profits to benefit distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission sent him on tour from Guilin through its counties to Yong, asked after hardships, acted first and reported later, and gave salt profits to help distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 嘉定初，差主管尚書吏部架閣文字，遷太學正，升博士。

translations.literal: In early Jiading he was appointed Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel Archive; he was moved to Director of the Imperial University and advanced to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jiading he was clerk in the Ministry of Personnel archive, then director of the Imperial University, then erudite.

sentences.zh: 轉對，首論主威奪而國勢輕；

translations.literal: Presenting at court, he first discussed that sovereign authority was seized and national strength lightened;
translations.idiomatic: At court he first argued that royal authority was slipping and national strength weakening;

sentences.zh: 次論士大夫寡廉隅、乏骨鯁，宜養天下剛毅果敢之氣；

translations.literal: next that scholar-officials lacked integrity and backbone and one should nurture the realm's firm, bold spirit;
translations.idiomatic: next that officials lacked integrity and spine and the court should nurture bold, upright spirit;

sentences.zh: 末論權臣用事，包苴成風，今舊習猶在，宜舉行先朝痛繩贓吏之法。

translations.literal: last that powerful ministers held power and gift-giving was rampant; old habits remain—one should enforce the former court's law of sternly punishing corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: last that powerful ministers and gift-giving still ruled and the court should enforce the old law against corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 謂太學風化首，童子科覆試胄子舍選，有挾勢者，中行力言于長，守法無秋豪私。

translations.literal: He said the Imperial University leads custom; in the Youth Examination the repeat examination of academy students and selected candidates—when some relied on influence, Zhongxing spoke forcefully to the director and upheld the law without the slightest private favor.
translations.idiomatic: He said the university sets the tone; when candidates relied on influence in the youth examination, Chai spoke firmly to the director and upheld the law without favor.

sentences.zh: 遷太常主簿，轉軍器監丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to Assistant Director of the Armaments Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to assistant director of the Armaments Directorate.

sentences.zh: 出知光州，嚴保伍，精閱習，增辟屯田，城壕營砦、器械糗糧，百爾具備，治行為淮右最。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Guangzhou, strictly maintained mutual-security groups, thoroughly drilled troops, expanded garrison farming, moats, camps, weapons, and provisions—all fully provided; his administration ranked first in Huai Right.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Guangzhou he tightened mutual-security groups, drilled troops thoroughly, expanded garrison farms, moats, camps, arms, and grain until all was ready—his record ranked first on the Huai right.

sentences.zh: 又條畫極邊、次邊緩急事宜上之朝廷，大概謂：「邊兵宜如蛇勢，首尾相應。

translations.literal: He also drew up urgent and routine measures for the outer and inner borders and submitted them to court, in general saying: "Border troops should be like a serpent, head and tail responding to each other.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted border plans to court, saying in essence, "Border troops should move like a serpent, head and tail answering each other.

sentences.zh: 草寇合兵大入，則鄰道援之；

translations.literal: When grass bandits unite in a great incursion, neighboring circuits aid;
translations.idiomatic: When bandits unite in force, neighboring circuits should aid;

sentences.zh: 分兵輕襲，則鄰郡援之。

translations.literal: when they divide forces for light raids, neighboring prefectures aid.
translations.idiomatic: when they raid lightly, neighboring prefectures should aid.

sentences.zh: 援兵既多，雖危不敗。」

translations.literal: With many relief troops, though in peril they will not be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: With ample relief, even in peril the line will hold."

sentences.zh: 又言：「淮、襄土豪丁壯，往者用兵，傾貲效力者，朝廷吝賞失信，宜亟加收拾，亦可激昂得其死力。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Stalwart household men of Huai and Xiang—in former campaigns those who spent wealth and strength, the court was stingy with rewards and broke faith; they should quickly be gathered in, and one can also stir them to die for the cause."
translations.idiomatic: He also said stalwart men of Huai and Xiang who spent wealth in past wars had been rewarded stingily; they should be won back quickly to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 遷西京轉運使兼提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was moved to Transport Commissioner of the Western Capital while also Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made transport commissioner of the Western Capital with concurrent duty as judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 中行謂襄陽乃自古必爭之地，備禦尤宜周密。

translations.literal: Zhongxing said Xiangyang was from antiquity a place armies must contest and defense should be especially tight.
translations.idiomatic: Chai said Xiangyang had always been a place armies must fight for and should be defended with special care.

sentences.zh: 時任邊寄者政令煩苛，日夜與民爭利，中行諷之，不聽。

translations.literal: At that time those holding border posts had harsh, tangled policies and day and night contended with the people for profit; Zhongxing admonished them but they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Border commanders then issued tangled orders and wrung profit from the people day and night; Chai admonished them in vain.

sentences.zh: 天方旱，盡捐酒稅，斥征官，黥務吏，甘澍隨至。

translations.literal: Heaven was just then dry; he entirely remitted liquor tax, dismissed tax officers, tattooed clerks who squeezed, and sweet rain followed at once.
translations.idiomatic: A drought had begun; he remitted liquor tax, dismissed tax officers, branded squeezing clerks, and timely rain followed.

sentences.zh: 官取鹽鈔贏過重，課日增，入中日寡，鈔日壅。

translations.literal: Officials took salt notes with excessive profit; daily levies rose while daily intake dwindled and notes clogged.
translations.idiomatic: Officials took excessive profit on salt notes; levies rose while intake fell and notes piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 中行揭示通衢，一錢不增，商賈大集。

translations.literal: Zhongxing posted notices on the main thoroughfare, adding not one cash; merchants gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Chai posted notices on the main roads, adding not a single cash; merchants flocked in.

sentences.zh: 改直秘閣、知襄陽兼京西帥，仍領漕事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Gentleman of the Secretariat, prefect of Xiangyang while also commander of Jingxi, still overseeing transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was made gentleman of the Secretariat, prefect of Xiangyang with command of Jingxi, still overseeing transport.

sentences.zh: 江陵戎司移屯襄州，兵政久馳。

translations.literal: The Jiangling military commission moved its encampment to Xiangzhou; military administration had long been lax.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangling military commission moved to Xiangzhou; military discipline had long slackened.

sentences.zh: 中行白於朝，考核軍實，舊額二萬二千人，存者才半，亟招補虛籍。

translations.literal: Zhongxing reported to court, examined true military strength—the old quota twenty-two thousand, those remaining only half—and urgently recruited to fill empty rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chai reported to court, audited the rolls—quota twenty-two thousand, barely half present—and urgently filled empty names.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷以節制之權歸帥司。

translations.literal: From this the court returned command authority to the commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the court returned command authority to the commander.

sentences.zh: 重劾李珙不法以懲貪守，時扈再興有功以厲宿將，上關朝廷，下關制閫。

translations.literal: He heavily impeached Li Gong's unlawfulness to punish greedy prefects; at that time Hu Zai had merit to encourage old generals—matters concerned both court and frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Li Gong's crimes to punish greedy prefects; when Hu Zai's merit needed honoring old generals, he reported to both court and frontier command.

sentences.zh: 遷江東轉運司判官，旋改湖南提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was moved to Transport Judge of Jiangdong and soon changed to Judicial Intendant of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made transport judge of Jiangdong and soon judicial intendant of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 豪家習殺人，或收養亡命，橫行江湖，一繩以法。

translations.literal: Powerful families were accustomed to killing; some kept fugitives and ranged across rivers and lakes—he bound them all by law.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families were used to murder; some harbored fugitives and terrorized the rivers—he bound them all by law.

sentences.zh: 華亭令貪虐，法從交疏薦之，中行笑曰：「此欲斷吾按章也。」

translations.literal: The magistrate of Huating was greedy and cruel; a law relative recommended him by connection; Zhongxing laughed and said: "This is meant to cut off my impeachment memorial."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Huating was greedy and cruel; a law relative recommended him through connections; Chai laughed, "They mean to stop my impeachment."

sentences.zh: 卒發其辜。

translations.literal: In the end he exposed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he exposed the man's crimes.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部郎官。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以立志啟迪君心，言好進、好同、好欺，士大夫風俗三敝。

translations.literal: With establishing resolve he enlightened the ruler's heart, speaking of the three abuses of the scholar-official world: eager advancement, eager conformity, and eager deceit.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to awaken the ruler's resolve and spoke of three abuses among officials: craving advancement, craving conformity, and craving deceit.

sentences.zh: 選曹法大壞，吏緣為奸，中行遇事持正，不為勢屈，由是銓綜平允。

translations.literal: The selection office's law was greatly broken and clerks used it for fraud; Zhongxing held to rectitude in affairs and did not bend to power; thereby appointments were fair.
translations.idiomatic: Selection law was badly broken and clerks preyed on it; Chai held firm and would not bend to power, and appointments became fair.

sentences.zh: 擢宗正少卿。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 上疏謂：「陛下初政則以剛德立治本，更化則以剛德除權奸，今者顧乃垂拱仰成，安于無為。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "When Your Majesty first took government you established the root with firm virtue; in the renewal you used firm virtue to remove powerful traitors; now you only lean back with folded hands and rest in non-action.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "At the start of your reign you rooted government in firm virtue; in renewal you used it to purge powerful traitors; now you lean back in repose and rest in non-action.

sentences.zh: 夫剛德實人主之大權，不可以久出而不收，覆轍在前，良可鑒也。」

translations.literal: Firm virtue is in truth the great power of the ruler; it cannot long be released and not drawn back; overturned cart ruts lie ahead—let that be a mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Firm virtue is the ruler's great power; it cannot long be let go and not reclaimed—the overturned cart ahead should be your mirror."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朝廷用人，外示涵洪而陰掩其跡，內用牢籠而微見其機，觀聽雖美，實無以大服天下之心。

translations.literal: He also said: "In employing men the court outwardly shows tolerance while secretly covering tracks, inwardly uses entanglement while slightly revealing schemes—hearing and sight are beautiful yet in truth cannot greatly satisfy hearts throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the court seemed tolerant outwardly while hiding tracks inwardly—appearances were fine yet could not truly satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 曩者更化，元氣復挽回矣。

translations.literal: Formerly in renewal, vital energy was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the earlier renewal, vital energy had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 比年欲求安靜，頗厭人言，於是臣下納說，非觀望則希合，非回緩則畏避，而面折廷諍之風未之多見，此任事大臣之責也。」

translations.literal: In recent years wishing for quiet, quite tired of men's words, thus subordinates offer counsel—if not watching and waiting then hoping to conform, if not evasive then fearful—and face-to-face remonstrance in court is not much seen; this is the duty of ministers who bear affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Lately, seeking quiet, the court has tired of speech; ministers either wait, conform, or dodge, and blunt remonstrance in open court is rare—this is the duty of chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Compiler of the National History and Revisionist of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as compiler of the National History and revisionist of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 孟春，大雨震電，雷雹交作，邊烽告急，至失地喪師，淮甸震洶。

translations.literal: In first spring, great rain, thunder, and lightning; hail mixed; border beacons reported emergency, even to lost land and lost armies; the Huai region shook and surged.
translations.idiomatic: In early spring came heavy rain, thunder, and hail; border beacons reported emergencies, even lost territory and lost armies; the Huai country shook.

sentences.zh: 中行亟奏內外二失，朝廷十憂，大要言：「今日之事，人主盡委天下以任一相，一相盡以天下謀之三數腹心，而舉朝之士相視以目，噤不敢言。

translations.literal: Zhongxing urgently memorialized on two failures within and without and ten worries of court, in general saying: "Today's affair: the ruler entirely entrusts the realm to one minister; one minister entirely plans the realm with three or four confidants; while the whole court looks on with eyes and dares not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Chai urgently memorialized on inner and outer failures and ten court worries, saying in essence, "Today the emperor entrusts all to one minister, that minister to a few confidants, and the whole court watches in silence.

sentences.zh: 甚至邊庭申請，久不即報，脫有闕誤，咎當誰執？」

translations.literal: Even border requests long go unanswered; if there is fault, who bears the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Even border requests go unanswered for long; if disaster comes, who bears blame?"

sentences.zh: 調秘書監、崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Secretariat and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 極論「往年以道學為偽學者，欲加遠竄，杜絕言語，使忠義士箝口結舌，天下之氣豈堪再沮壞如此耶？」

translations.literal: He strongly discussed: "In former years those who called the Learning of the Way false wished to banish it far, cut off speech, and make loyal, righteous men seal lips and knot tongues—can the realm's spirit bear to be crushed again like this?"
translations.idiomatic: He spoke forcefully: "Those who called the Learning of the Way false wanted to exile it, silence speech, and make loyal men seal their lips—can the realm's spirit be crushed again?"

sentences.zh: 又謂：「欲結人心，莫若去貪吏；

translations.literal: He also said: "To bind human hearts, nothing is better than removing greedy officials;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "To bind hearts, nothing beats removing greedy officials;

sentences.zh: 欲去貪吏，莫若清朝廷。

translations.literal: to remove greedy officials, nothing is better than clarifying the court.
translations.idiomatic: to remove greedy officials, nothing beats clarifying the court.

sentences.zh: 大臣法則小臣廉，在高位者以身率下，則州縣小吏何恃而敢為？」

translations.literal: When great ministers uphold law, petty ministers are honest; those in high position lead those below by example—on what would prefectural and county petty clerks rely to dare act?"
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers uphold the law, lesser officials grow honest; when those above lead by example, what could petty clerks rely on to misbehave?"

sentences.zh: 又論內治外患，辨君子小人，大略謂：「執政、侍從、台諫、給舍之選，與三衙、京尹之除，皆朝廷大綱所在，故其人必出人主之親擢，則權不下移。

translations.literal: He also discussed internal governance and external peril, distinguishing gentleman and petty man, in general saying: "Selection of administrators, attendants, remonstrators, and drafting officers, and appointments of the Three Bureaus and capital magistrate—all are great outlines of court; therefore the men must come from the ruler's personal elevation, then power does not shift downward.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke on domestic rule and foreign threat and on gentlemen versus petty men: "Appointments to the council, palace, remonstrance, and drafting offices and to the Three Bureaus and capital magistracies are the court's main pillars; their holders should come from the emperor's own choice so power does not slip downward.

sentences.zh: 今或私謁，或請見，或數月之前先定，或舉朝之人不識。

translations.literal: Now some by private audience, some by requesting audience, some fixed months beforehand, some unknown to the whole court.
translations.idiomatic: Now some win posts by private audiences, some by begging an audience, some fixed months in advance, some unknown to the whole court.

sentences.zh: 附會者進，爭為妾婦之道，則天下國家之利害安危，非惟己不敢言，亦且並絕人言矣。

translations.literal: Those who attach advance; they compete in the way of concubine and wife—then the gain, loss, safety, and peril of realm and state: not only do they themselves not dare speak, they also cut off others' speech entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers advance and vie like subservient wives—then who dares speak of the realm's safety? They silence themselves and silence everyone else.

sentences.zh: 大臣為附會之說所誤，邊境之臣實遁者掩以為誣，真怯者譽以為勇，金帛滿前，是非交亂，以欺廟堂，以欺陛下。

translations.literal: Great ministers are misled by the talk of flatterers; border officers who truly flee are covered as slander, those truly cowardly are praised as brave; gold and silk fill before them, right and wrong tangle—deceiving the ancestral temple and deceiving Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers are misled by flatterers; border officers who flee are called slandered, cowards praised as brave; gold and silk pile before them, right and wrong tangle—they deceive the ancestral temple and the throne.

sentences.zh: 願明詔大臣，絕私意，布公道。」

translations.literal: I wish an edict to great ministers to end private intent and spread public justice."
translations.idiomatic: I beg an edict commanding great ministers to end private aims and uphold public justice."

sentences.zh: 進秘閣修撰、知贛州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Secret Archive and made prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Academician of the Secret Archive and appointed prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢盜有方，境內清肅。

translations.literal: Skilled in repelling bandits, within the borders all was clear and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Once banditry was mastered, the prefecture grew calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 丐祠得請，以言罷。

translations.literal: He begged a temple post and was granted it, then was dismissed because of critics.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a sinecure and received it, then lost office after criticism.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，以右文殿修撰主管南京鴻慶宮，賜金帶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne he was made Academician of the Right Culture Hall in charge of the Nanjing Hongqing Palace and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne he was made Academician of the Right Culture Hall in charge of the Nanjing Hongqing Palace and granted a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 所著有《易系集傳》、《書集傳》、《詩講義》、《論語童蒙說》。

translations.literal: His works include Appended Commentary on the Changes, Appended Commentary on the Documents, Exposition of the Odes, and Explication of the Analects for Young Learners.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Appended Commentary on the Changes, Appended Commentary on the Documents, Exposition of the Odes, and Explication of the Analects for Young Learners.

sentences.zh: 李孟傳

translations.literal: Li Mengchuan
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchuan

sentences.zh: 李孟傳，字文授，資政殿學士光季子也。

translations.literal: Li Mengchuan, styled Wenshou, was son of Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance Li Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengchuan, whose courtesy name was Wenshou, was the son of Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance Li Guang.

sentences.zh: 光謫嶺海，孟傳才六歲，奉母居鄉，刻志於學。

translations.literal: When Guang was banished to the southern sea, Mengchuan was only six; he attended his mother in the village and carved his will on study.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guang was banished to the southern sea, Mengchuan was only six; he stayed with his mother in the village and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 賀允中、徐度皆奇之，而曾幾妻以其孫。

translations.literal: He Yi and Xu Du both thought him extraordinary, and Zeng Ji's wife gave him her grandson in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He Yi and Xu Du both marveled at him, and Zeng Ji's wife betrothed her grandson to him.

sentences.zh: 龍大淵黜為浙東總管，知孟傳為名門子，解後必就語，孟傳正色辭之。

translations.literal: Long Dayuan was demoted to Eastern Zhe chief steward; knowing Mengchuan was a famous minister's son, whenever they met by chance he would surely seek conversation; Mengchuan sternly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Long Dayuan was demoted to Eastern Zhe chief steward; knowing Mengchuan was a famous minister's son, he always sought talk when they met; Mengchuan coldly refused.

sentences.zh: 幹辦江東提刑司，易浙東常平司。

translations.literal: Planning officer of the Jiangdong Judicial Commission; transferred to the Eastern Zhe Ever-Normal Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as planner on the Jiangdong Judicial Commission, then on the Eastern Zhe Ever-Normal Commission.

sentences.zh: 母喪，免，調江山縣丞，棄去，監南嶽廟、行在編估局，未上，改楚州司戶參軍，單車赴官。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangshan, he abandoned it; supervised the Southern Sacred Mountain Temple and the Capital Valuation Bureau—had not reported—was changed to Military Administrator of Chuzhou and went to office alone in a single cart.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office; offered assistant magistrate of Jiangshan, he declined; was put in charge of the Southern Sacred Mountain Temple and the capital valuation bureau but never reported; was reassigned military administrator of Chuzhou and went alone in a single cart.

sentences.zh: 公退，閉戶讀《易》。

translations.literal: After public business he closed his door and read the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: After office hours he shut his door and read the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 郡守、部使者不敢待以屬吏。

translations.literal: The prefect and circuit commissioners dared not treat him as a subordinate clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and circuit commissioners dared not treat him as a junior clerk.

sentences.zh: 徐積墓在境內，蕪沒既久，加葺之。

translations.literal: Xu Ji's tomb was within the jurisdiction, long overgrown and ruined; he restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji's tomb in the district had long lain ruined; he restored it.

sentences.zh: 修復陳公塘，有灌溉之利。

translations.literal: He restored the Chen Gong Pond, which had the benefit of irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Chen Gong Pond, which brought irrigation benefits.

sentences.zh: 知象山縣，守薦為邑最，從官多合薦之，主管官告院，與同列上封事，請詣北宮，又移書宰相。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Xiangshan County; the prefect recommended him as the best county; many court officials jointly recommended him; he supervised the Court of Honors and with colleagues submitted a sealed memorial asking to visit the Northern Palace and also wrote the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xiangshan the prefect rated him the best county; many at court recommended him; he supervised the Court of Honors and with colleagues submitted a sealed memorial to visit the Northern Palace and wrote the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遷將作監主簿。

translations.literal: He was moved to Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was made registrar of the Directorate of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚初當國，適大侵，遣孟傳按視江、池、鄂三大軍所屯積粟，道除太府丞。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu was just then directing the state; a great famine occurred; he sent Mengchuan to inspect stored grain at the three great armies stationed on the Yangzi, Chi, and E; on the road he was made Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu was directing the state a great famine struck; he sent Mengchuan to inspect grain stores of the three great armies on the Yangzi, Chi, and E; en route he was made assistant director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 既復命，汝愚去國，黨論起，而孟傳奉使無失指，面對言：「比以使事往返四千里，所過民生困窮，衣食不贍。

translations.literal: After he reported back, Ruyu left office and factional debate arose; yet Mengchuan on his mission made no misstep; facing the throne he said: "Recently on embassy I went and returned four thousand li; wherever I passed the people's lives were impoverished and they lacked food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After he reported, Zhao Ruyu left office and factional strife erupted; yet Mengchuan's mission drew no blame; at audience he said, "On this embassy I traveled four thousand li and everywhere saw people without food or clothing.

sentences.zh: 國之安危，以民為本，今根本既虛，形勢俱見，保邦之慮，宜勤聖念。」

translations.literal: The safety of the state takes the people as root; now the root is already hollow and the situation fully appears—thought for preserving the state should stir the sage mind."
translations.idiomatic: The state's safety rests on the people; the root is hollow and the danger plain—preserving the realm should weigh on the emperor's mind."

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄連逐留正及汝愚，太府簿吳璹與侂胄有連姻，因言台諫將論朱熹，孟傳奮然曰：「如此則士大夫爭之，鼎鑊且不避。」

translations.literal: At that time Han Tuozhou in succession drove out Liu Zheng and Ruyu; Treasury Assistant Wu Shan was related to Tuozhou by marriage and therefore said the remonstrance office would impeach Zhu Xi; Mengchuan said fervently: "If so, scholar-officials will contend—even the cauldron and axe they will not avoid."
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was then driving out Liu Zheng and Zhao Ruyu; treasury assistant Wu Shan, related to Tuozhou by marriage, said the censorate would attack Zhu Xi; Mengchuan flared up: "Then scholars will fight—even facing cauldron and axe they will not flinch."

sentences.zh: 兼考功郎。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 復因對言：「國家長育人才，猶天地之於植物，滋液滲漉，待其既成而後足以供大廈之用。

translations.literal: Again facing the throne he said: "The state long nurtures talent like heaven and earth with plants—moisture seeps and drips, waiting until they are formed before they suffice for the great hall.
translations.idiomatic: Again at audience he said, "The state nurtures talent as heaven and earth nurture plants—moisture must seep in until they are formed before they can bear the great hall.

sentences.zh: 今士大夫皆有苟進之心，治功未優，功能尚薄，而意已馳騖於台閣，不稍有以扶持正飭之，其敝將甚。」

translations.literal: Now scholar-officials all have a mind of careless advancement; governing achievement is not yet excellent, ability is still thin, yet their thoughts already race toward the high offices—if they are not somewhat supported and corrected, the harm will be great."
translations.idiomatic: Officials now crave quick promotion; achievement is thin yet minds already race toward high office—without correction the harm will be grave."

sentences.zh: 又言：「武舉及軍士比試，專取其力，臨敵難以必勝。

translations.literal: He also said: "Military examinations and comparison tests of soldiers take strength alone—in facing the enemy it is hard to be sure of victory.
translations.idiomatic: He also said military exams and troop trials test strength alone—hardly a sure win in battle.

sentences.zh: 唐世取人由步射、弓弩以至馬射，各以其中之多寡為等級，宜採取行之。」

translations.literal: The Tang in taking men proceeded from foot archery and crossbow to horse archery, each graded by how many hits—this should be adopted and carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Tang recruitment graded men from foot archery and crossbow to mounted archery by hits—that method should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄與孟傳故，嘗致侂胄意，孟傳謝曰：「行年六十，去意已決。」

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was old acquaintance with Mengchuan and once conveyed Tuozhou's intent; Mengchuan declined, saying: "I am sixty years old; my mind to leave is already settled."
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou, an old acquaintance, once conveyed his wishes; Mengchuan declined: "I am sixty; my mind to leave is set."

sentences.zh: 侂胄慚而退。

translations.literal: Tuozhou withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou withdrew ashamed.

sentences.zh: 請外，知江州，獄訟止息。

translations.literal: He asked to go outside and became prefect of Jiangzhou; lawsuits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the capital and became prefect of Jiangzhou; lawsuits died down.

sentences.zh: 侂胄不悅。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was displeased.

sentences.zh: 丐歸，復知處州。

translations.literal: He begged to return home and again became prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return home and again held Chuzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西提點刑獄，改江東提舉常平，移福建。

translations.literal: He was moved to Judicial Intendant of Guangxi, changed to Intendant of Jiangdong Ever-Normal Granaries, then transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judicial intendant of Guangxi, then intendant of Jiangdong Ever-Normal Granaries, then transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 詔入對，首論用人宜先氣節後才能，益招徠忠讜以扶正論。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to report; he first discussed that in employing men one should put integrity before ability and further recruit loyal remonstrance to straighten discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to report, he said men should be chosen for integrity before talent and loyal remonstrance should be recruited to straighten public debate.

sentences.zh: 故人有在政府者，折簡問勞勤甚，孟傳逆知其意，即謝曰：「孤蹤久不造朝，獲一望清光而去，幸矣。」

translations.literal: An old friend in government sent a note asking after him with great solicitude; Mengchuan guessed his intent and at once declined, saying: "My solitary track has long not visited court; to obtain one glimpse of clear radiance and depart is already fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: An old friend in government sent a warm note; Mengchuan guessed his intent and declined: "I have long stayed away from court; one glimpse of the throne before I go is fortune enough."

sentences.zh: 對畢即出關。

translations.literal: When the audience was finished he at once left the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended he left the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 至閩，大饑，發廩勸分，民無流莩。

translations.literal: Reaching Fujian, great famine struck; he opened granaries and urged sharing; the people had no corpses along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fujian in great famine, he opened granaries and urged sharing; no corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，就遷提點刑獄，移江東，又辭。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed he was moved on site to judicial intendant, then to Jiangdong, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed he was moved on site to judicial intendant, then to Jiangdong, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠，其親故也，人謂進用其時矣，卒歸使節，角巾還第。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was his kinsman by marriage; people said his hour to advance had come; in the end he returned the envoy's credentials, put on a scholar's headcloth, and went home.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was a kinsman; men said his time had come; he returned the envoy's credentials, put on plain dress, and went home.

sentences.zh: 再奉祠，以倉部郎召，又辭。

translations.literal: Twice granted temple posts; summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Twice granted sinecures; summoned as director in the Ministry of Revenue and again declined.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提點刑獄，未數月，申前請，章再上，加直秘閣，移江東，不赴，主管明道宮。

translations.literal: Moved to Judicial Intendant of Eastern Zhe; within not many months he repeated his former request; the memorial came again; given Direct Secretariat; moved to Jiangdong—did not go; put in charge of the Mingdao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Made judicial intendant of Eastern Zhe; within months he repeated his request; the memorial came again; given Direct Secretariat; offered Jiangdong—he did not go; put in charge of the Mingdao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 進直寶謨閣，致仕，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: Advanced to Gentleman of the Direct Hall of Treasured Planning, retired, died at the age of eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to Gentleman of the Direct Hall of Treasured Planning, he retired and died at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 常誡其子孫曰：「安身莫若無競，修己莫若自保。

translations.literal: He often admonished his sons and grandsons: "To settle the body nothing is better than not competing; to cultivate the self nothing is better than self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his sons and grandsons: "To settle your person, nothing beats refusing to compete; to cultivate yourself, nothing beats guarding your integrity.

sentences.zh: 守道則福至，求祿則辱來。」

translations.literal: Uphold the Way and blessing comes; seek salary and disgrace comes."
translations.idiomatic: Uphold the Way and blessing follows; chase salary and disgrace follows."

sentences.zh: 有《磐溪集》、《宏詞類稿》、《左氏說》、《讀史》、《雜志》、《記善》、《記異》等書行世。

translations.literal: His Panxi Collection, Grand Rhetoric Drafts, Zuoshi Exposition, Reading History, Miscellanies, Recording Good, and Recording Strange and others circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Panxi Collection, Grand Rhetoric Drafts, Zuoshi Exposition, Reading History, Miscellanies, Recording Good, and Recording Strange circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古之君子，出處不齊，同歸於是而已。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Ancient gentlemen differed in going out and staying in yet alike returned to this.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Ancient gentlemen differed in whether they served or withdrew, yet alike aimed at what was right.

sentences.zh: 辛棄疾知大義而歸宋。

translations.literal: Xin Qiji knew great principle and returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji knew the greater duty and returned to Song.

sentences.zh: 何異篤實君子，而切諫光宗朝重華宮。

translations.literal: He Yi was a solid, true gentleman who earnestly remonstrated on Guangzong's neglect of Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He Yi was a solid, true gentleman who earnestly remonstrated when Guangzong neglected Chonghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 柴中行寧不校臨川之試，終不肯自言非程頤偽學。

translations.literal: Chai Zhongxing would rather not dispute the Linchuan examination yet to the end would not declare himself non-false in Cheng Yi's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zhongxing would not fuss over the Linchuan examination yet never declared Cheng Yi's learning false.

sentences.zh: 劉爚表章朱熹《四書》以備勸講，衛道之功莫大焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yue displayed Zhu Xi's Four Books for lecture preparation—the merit of guarding the Way was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue promoted Zhu Xi's Four Books for imperial lectures—his merit in guarding the Way was immense.

sentences.zh: 李孟傳所立不愧其父。

translations.literal: What Li Mengchuan established did not shame his father.
translations.idiomatic: What Li Mengchuan stood for did not shame his father.

sentences.zh: 至於劉宰飄然遠引，屢征不起，所謂鴻飛冥冥者耶。

translations.literal: As for Liu Zai, drifting far and withdrawn, repeatedly summoned yet not rising—what is called the wild goose flying in the deep dark, is it not he?
translations.idiomatic: As for Liu Zai, drifting far off, summoned again and again yet never coming—is this not the wild goose flying in the deep dark?
